a5.speaker: Sara Beysolow-Nyanti, Liberia's Foreign Minister
a5.name: Sara Beysolow-Nyanti
a5.title: Liberia's Foreign Minister
a5.speech: Is urging the media and the public to refrain from publishing the names of Liberians allegedly facing deportation by the United States government ; emphasized that neither the Foreign Ministry nor the Liberian Embassy in Washington, D.C, has received any official communication regarding the circulating lists ; noted that the Liberian government is actively engaged in dialogue with officials of the U.S. Embassy in Monrovia to address the situation ; also noted that President Joseph Boakai is concerned about the reports of deportation and is preparing to write a letter to U.S. President Donald Trump seeking clarifications ; disclosed plans to travel to the United States by late February to meet with the U.S. Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, to discuss the matter.

a585.speaker: Mahmoud Abdirahman Beenabeene, Federal Government of Somalia Minister of Planning and Investment
a585.name: Mahmoud Abdirahman Beenabeene
a585.title: Federal Government of Somalia Minister of Planning and Investment
a585.speech: After expressing thanks, underlined that most of this grant money will be used by the Government to develop health, education and good governance in the areas the Government liberated from the enemy Al-Shabaab.

a585.speaker: Bihi Iman Ige, Federal Government of Somalia Minister of Finance
a585.name: Bihi Iman Ige
a585.title: Federal Government of Somalia Minister of Finance
a585.speech: Thanked USAID and said that this grant is the tax paid by the American people, and likewise he called on the Somali people to pay taxes so that dependence on aid coming from abroad can be avoided.

a585.speaker: Catie Lott, Head of the USAID Office in Somalia
a585.name: Catie Lott
a585.title: Head of the USAID Office in Somalia
a585.speech: Said that this agreement reflects the level reached by the cooperation between the Government of the United States and Somalia, and she indicated that she would like to see the good results that come from the grant they provided being invested in the regions.

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC) (press conference statement)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC) (press conference statement)
a694.speech: "Yesterday, President Joseph N. Boikai delivered his second State of the Nation's Address and this is our official response. We choose to speak directly this time to the Liberian people because of the grave instability and uncertainty that now hang over our democracy and economy. Our nation is in crisis. The state of the nation is weak, divided and polarized, and this was evident yesterday, when about eight Senators, more than 25 representatives, and the entire Supreme Court bench boycotted President Boakai's SONA. This is deeply troubling." ; "Liberia is in decline. The democratic and economic gains we made in the last six years are being eroded. We now see the Unity Party trapped in the very lies they sold the Liberian people to get elected. There is too much confusion and disunity in the land. All of these require a spoken response that expresses the raw emotions and feelings of our people during these turbulent times."

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: Made it clear that President George Manneh Weah conceded political power to then President-elect Joseph N. Boakai several days before the National Elections Commission completed the announcement of election results, insisting that in conceding the then incumbent President Weah demonstrated an act of extreme patriotism and that their standard bearer broke ranks with Liberia's bitter past of contested elections ; "He signaled the dawn of a new day in Liberian peace and democracy. Where before others believed that our democracy was weak and fragile, President Weah showed that Liberia too was capable of democratic and electoral strength we see in advanced democracies such as the United States, Britain or Germany. President Weah handed President Boakai a peaceful country and democracy, a Liberia in which the rule of law was respected, in which no president, legislator, or justice was above the law."

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: Indicated that one year after the most peaceful democratic transfer of power Liberia now lies in a democratic and rule-of-law mess, because the Unity Party administration is teaching Liberians that the rule of law has no meaning and that the law is whatever the President and his legislative friends say it is ; "Our fellow citizens, because the rule of law is so important to the working of any society - to how citizens' rights to justice, healthcare, or education are nourished and protected; and to how foreigners and investors perceive the role the law plays in protecting their investments - the Unity Party's destruction of the rule of law has now affected every aspect of Liberian social and political life since President George M. Weah left office." ; "Today, citizens are confused as to where the country is headed under Joseph Boakai. Today, citizens are beaten and wounded if they dare to get into the streets to exercise their constitutional rights to free speech and assembly. Today, whatever the Supreme Court says is no longer the law. Today, opposition personalities and former government officials are being witch-hunted and unjustly imprisoned. Today, the country has both a constitutionally elected speaker and a quote-unquote majority block Speaker who was illegally selected. Despite these violations, the Executive has imposed this illegally selected Speaker upon the Government and people of Liberia, while at the same time seeking the resignation of the duly elected Speaker. What a mockery of democracy and the rule of law!"

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: Asked rhetorically "How did Liberians get into this big political mess?" before stating that "we got here because the Unity Party packaged a massive bundle of lies and sold those lies to the Liberian people. They lied that harmonization was bad and upon taking office they would have reversed it immediately; that the CDC was the importer of drugs in the Country and they would have solved the drug problems in six months; they said that no car was going to get stuck in the mud in the first 100 days of the Boakai administration; they promised Liberians never to use private jet for presidential travels; they promised to bring down the prices of basic commodities in one year; and of course, they said they were going to bring down the US dollar- Liberian dollar exchange rate down to its lowest." ; emphasised that "As if this was not enough during the campaign, President Boakai repeated many of these promises in his first State of the Nation address", adding "One year after falsely raising the hopes of the Liberian people, the reality has now set in for the Unity Party" ; said the 'kush' the UP was supposed to stop has now grown into Zombie and satellite drugs, that in the first 150 days cars were stuck in mud more than ever before, and that President Boakai is now using private jets for domestic as well as international travel.

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: On the economy, pointed out that "today the price of basic commodities has not just increased, but the UP Government has admitted in the illegally passed 2025 National Budget that the exchange rate may reach as high as LRD 219 to US$1.00 in 2025. The economic reality we present above shows that the 'country is hard,' that the 'Rescue Mission has now become the Excuse Mission' and that Liberians should prepare for the worst economic situation in 2025," adding that Boakai's speech "was packed with misinformation in so many areas" ; "First, the Government says it collected $734 million in total revenue last year but spent on US$661.4 million. This means, we have $72.6 million of surplus that the Government should declare in the 2025 budget as the CDC administration used to do. But we know that the 2025 budget has no surplus or balance brought forward. So, two things are possible. Either the US$ 72.6 million was blown off in massive act of corruption or everything the president said about 2024 revenue was false and misleading." ; "Second, the President said that he decreased the price of rice. This one, we leave them with the Liberian people to judge. It was Liberians who were paying LR$3,100 for a 25kg bag of rice when the UP took over in January 2024, and who are now paying LR$3,500 as we speak." ; "Third, Mr. President, harmonization is still the prevailing policy in Liberia" ; "Fourth, information that 6,000 ghosts were removed from the payroll is misleading. The Unity Party has provided misinformation to the International Monetary Fund on this. The maximum number of ghost workers on the existing Government payroll cannot be more than 1000 persons. So, the maximum that can be saved due to ghost removal is about $1.8 million." ; and fifth, that the international climate financing mentioned in the speech - the US$25 million West Point/Monrovia Metropolitan Climate Resilience Project financed by the Green Climate Fund - was secured by the CDC administration: "Let the UP not take credit for a project they did not initiate. Mr. President your people misinform you."

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: Said that in 2018 it was the CDC that inherited a broken economy, with declining international aid, underperforming domestic revenue, and a two-payroll system that widened inequality, and that despite these challenges its administration achieved a number of feats in its first year - construction of more than 75 kilometers of community roads; placing more than 2,300 health workers on the Government payroll; increasing the salary of medical doctors from US$700 to US$2000; keeping the price of a 25kg bag of rice at US$13; sending more than 20 medical doctors for training abroad; declaring free tuition for public university students and free WASSCE for high school students; breaking ground for Military 14 Hospital; launching the Pro-Poor Agenda for Transformation; and digitizing registration at the University of Liberia ; thanked President Boakai for acknowledging that his government is building on the foundation laid by the Pro-Poor Agenda for Prosperity and Development (PAPD) under President George Manneh Weah ; said the foundation handed over included increased domestic revenue of US$640 million, a stabilised exchange rate and 10 percent inflation, harmonisation reducing the wage bill by US$32 million, Net International Reserves of US$240 million, a 25kg bag of rice held at US$13 for more than four years, an economic growth rate of more than 4.5 percent, and a declining poverty profile ; "We handed the unity party completed road works from Ganta to Saclepia, and major contracts from Tapeta to Toe Town, and Town Toe to Zwedru, with all financing and secured. We also handed UP the Fish Town-Zwedru corridor contract and financing frameworks. For our urban beautification and infrastructure improvement, we handed the unity party the SKD Boulevard, and the ministerial complex overpass contracts and framework. We also handed the UP the RIA road corridor. We handed the UP a completed central Monrovia water supply project and revenue generation infrastructure. We handed the UP 10-year World Bank financing for electricity transformation; the CDC passed the MCC scorecard three times, paving the way for Liberia's Compact eligibility. In contrast, the UP handed the CDC a weak MCC eligibility database in 2018 which led to Liberia failing the scorecard."

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: Charged the Unity Party Government with mismanagement of the national budget, saying it has resulted in severe inequities in resource allocation, with senior government officials enjoying exorbitant allowances and benefits while healthcare, agriculture and education remain critically underfunded ; "When the data finally comes in, we will see that budget execution for 2024 has been a disaster. Critical entities at the frontline of service delivery, especially in health and education, receiving as low as 50 percent of their budgetary allocation," adding that the nation's 23 public referral hospitals, which serve over 5.2 million citizens, lack essential medical supplies and critical services and have unpaid health workers ; "For the Unity Party, budget execution is about personal benefits and allowances. The UP uses the budget to ensure Government officials receive large amounts of gas coupons, scratch cards, and other benefits. Under the CDC, these benefits were cut to make room for spending that impacted the mass of Liberians who do not work for the Government."

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: Noted that 2024 saw no new foreign direct investment and no serious effort to resolve business climate challenges, and that what the nation saw instead was 'investment by showmanship' ; "Investment is not showmanship, the attempt to impress Liberians that the President has external relations and is about to bring investments because of his personality. We have seen a parade of deceptive announcements that were supposed to impress Liberians that the Unity Party was about the solve the country's investment challenge. These were all deceptive." ; cited the HPX/Guma Africa Group 'investment deal' announced on February 20 promising $3 billion to $5 billion for the Liberty Corridor which has not materialised; the July 15 parade of 285 yellow earth-moving machines and dump trucks for which there was no signed contract, no formal agreement and no financial commitment, a serious violation of procurement laws in which machines valued at US$80 million were really worth around US$20 million with the remaining US$60 million being kickbacks for officials of Government; the June 24, 2024 parading of two 'Marcopolo' buses with promises that 300 more would follow in 40 days; and the September announcement of a $3 billion memorandum for an oil refinery in Buchanan after the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, when the grants were roughly US$28 million, the debt waiver a mere US$900,000 and the food assistance package less than US$5 million ; and the December 19, 2024 claim of a $500 million MCC grant, saying "What Liberia had witnessed was yet another act in the administration's theater of deception" and that within its first year the UP administration has repeatedly used misinformation as a political tool.

a694.speaker: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.name: Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC)
a694.speech: "Our fellow citizens, the CDC welcomes the fight against corruption but such a fight cannot be on a selective basis", saying the UP Government has shown no serious commitment to fighting corruption and its current fight pertains to witch-hunting former officials of the CDC administration where there is no basis, while several cases of corruption involving the National Port Authority, the Liberia Revenue Authority, the Ministry of Public Works, the LRRRC, the Ministry of Commerce, the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Central Bank of Liberia, the Liberia Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Agriculture, involving tens of millions of US dollars, remain unaddressed.

a694.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia (State of the Nation Address)
a694.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a694.title: President of Liberia (State of the Nation Address)
a694.speech: On Monday, January 27, painted an adorable picture of the Liberian economy amid applauses, claiming amiable business environment, growth and lower inflation; said he decreased the price of rice; said that "people were facing extreme hardship because of harmonization"; said 6,000 ghosts were removed from the payroll; said the Government collected $734 million in total revenue last year but spent US$661.4 million; and said very little about what the Unity Party achieved under its 100-day programme or in its first year, while acknowledging that his government is building on the foundation laid by the Pro-Poor Agenda for Prosperity and Development under President George Manneh Weah.

a694.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (statement)
a694.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (statement)
a694.speech: Released a statement calmly dismantling the government's claim: there was no grant, no $500 million, and no MCC compact funding, and eligibility does not guarantee a Compact as the government propagated.

a694.speaker: Unity Party Government of Liberia (announcements)
a694.name: Unity Party Government of Liberia (announcements)
a694.speech: Announced on February 20 an ambitious partnership with HPX and Guma Africa Group promising an investment of $3 billion to $5 billion to develop the Liberty Corridor; claimed on June 24, 2024 to have found the solution to Liberia's transportation crisis, parading two buses billed as samples from the Brazilian manufacturer "Marcopolo" with promises that 300 more would follow in just 40 days; announced in September, on returning from the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, a $3 billion memorandum for an oil refinery in Buchanan, Grand Bassa County; and claimed on December 19, 2024 to have secured a $500 million grant from the Millennium Challenge Corporation ; when pressed on the yellow machines, the President offered only a vague explanation, attributing the initiative to a casual conversation with an unnamed "friend".

a694.speaker: World Bank 2024 economic report
a694.name: World Bank 2024 economic report
a694.speech: Cited by the CDC as showing a declining poverty profile handed to the Unity Party, while the same report for the year 2017 showed the CDC inherited an increasing poverty profile in 2018.

a810.speaker: Ontiretse Letlhare, National Coordinator of the National AIDS and Health Promotion Agency (NAHPA)
a810.name: Ontiretse Letlhare
a810.title: National Coordinator of the National AIDS and Health Promotion Agency (NAHPA)
a810.speech: Expressed concern about the news. “We are aware of the US administration’s executive order to withdraw foreign aid but have not yet been formally briefed,” he said. “What we are doing is seeking clarity from our development partners, and I can assure you that efforts are ongoing.” ; acknowledged that the loss of US support is a severe blow, particularly for civil society organisations that are instrumental in Botswana’s HIV/AIDS response; however Letlhare was eager to calm fears, expressing confidence that the government would take the necessary measures to mitigate the impact.

a810.speaker: American government (notification to Botswana civil society organisations)
a810.name: American government (notification to Botswana civil society organisations)
a810.speech: Has already notified Botswana’s civil society organisations of the funding cuts, instructing them to “stop all work, not incur any new costs, and cancel as many outstanding obligations as possible”.

a810.speaker: Cindy Kelemi, Chairperson of BOCONGO (Botswana Council of Non-Governmental Organisations)
a810.name: Cindy Kelemi
a810.title: Chairperson of BOCONGO (Botswana Council of Non-Governmental Organisations)
a810.speech: Has described the US decision as “a disaster”. She elaborated: “This is a major setback for our HIV/AIDS response and the progress we’ve worked so hard to achieve. Civil society organisations are in a state of panic, with many facing closure, job losses, and the risk of our HIV/AIDS efforts falling into disarray.” ; cited Tebelopele, an NGO that provides antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 400 to 500 patients, as an example of those left in limbo by the abrupt cessation of operations and funding; said BOCONGO is planning to meet and petition the government “to fill the gap, at least temporarily, while strategising on long-term sustainable solutions”.

a810.speaker: Dr Edward Maganu, public health expert
a810.name: Dr Edward Maganu
a810.title: public health expert
a810.speech: Emphasised the broader implications of the US foreign aid cuts, including America’s withdrawal from the World Health Organisation (WHO). “The role of WHO in global health is critical, and the US has been its largest contributor,” he said. “Suddenly stopping that support will have devastating effects on international health efforts, including polio eradication and HIV/AIDS control.”

a810.speaker: Dr Edward Maganu, public health expert
a810.name: Dr Edward Maganu
a810.title: public health expert
a810.speech: Expressed the hope that Botswana, as an upper-middle-income country, will manage the impact to some extent. “Compared to other African countries, Botswana is less dependent on aid,” he noted. “Programmes like those funded by PEPFAR will suffer, but the country generally finances its own development. While there will be suffering, I believe Botswana can hold its own.”

a810.speaker: Kennedy Mupeli, Programme Director at the Centre for Youth of Hope (CEYOHO)
a810.name: Kennedy Mupeli
a810.title: Programme Director at the Centre for Youth of Hope (CEYOHO)
a810.speech: “This is a life-and-death matter for some,” he told The Botswana Gazette. “I don’t understand why the government hasn’t released a statement to address the panic within civil society and people living with HIV/AIDS.” ; vividly recalled how, during every funding application process, donors would always emphasise the importance of sustainability and inquire about long-term plans to maintain the initiatives.

a810.speaker: David Ngele, the first Motswana to go public about his HIV-positive status
a810.name: David Ngele
a810.title: the first Motswana to go public about his HIV-positive status
a810.speech: Called the US decision “a wake-up call for Botswana to establish sustainable strategies in its fight against HIV/AIDS.”

a810.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a810.name: Duma Boko
a810.title: President of Botswana
a810.speech: Recently praised Trump’s foreign policy stance in an interview with the international media, calling the American president “a positive influence on global diplomacy”. Boko asserted: “Trump brings robust diplomacy and is good for world peace. We flatter each other too much. He calls it as he sees it.”

a810.speaker: Dr Phenyo Butale, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Botswana
a810.name: Dr Phenyo Butale
a810.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Botswana
a810.speech: Had not responded to Gazette questions before publishing.

a826.speaker: Sources privy to the incident (anonymous)
a826.name: Sources privy to the incident (anonymous)
a826.speech: Told SaharaReporters that the home was stripped bare as the burglars “took everything from the house”; “The burglary took place at the quarters for Supreme Court justices in Maitama. It occurred over the Christmas holidays and Dattijo was travelling out of the country at the time.”

a826.speaker: Muhammad Dattijo, retired Justice of the Supreme Court of Nigeria
a826.name: Muhammad Dattijo
a826.title: retired Justice of the Supreme Court of Nigeria
a826.speech: Described the apex court as rotten and characterised by filth, lamenting that it had been pervaded by bribery and perversion of justice, and adding that it was dangerous for two out of the six geopolitical zones of the country to be excluded from the bench of the Supreme Court hearing appeals on the presidential election ; lamenting that the appointments of judicial officers have been political, selfish and sectional, he said: “It is asserted that the process of appointment to judicial positions is deliberately conducted to give undue advantage to the children, spouses and mistresses of serving and retired judges and managers of judicial offices. At the Court of Appeal, it is asserted, presiding justices are now being appointed out of turn. And there is the further issue of the unpredictable nature of recent decisions of the courts as well. A number of respected senior members of the bar inter alia, citing Ahmed Lawan, the former President of the Senate and Imo governorship appeals, claim that decisions of even the apex court have become unpredictable. It is difficult to understand how and where, by these decisions, the judicial pendulum swings. It was not so before, they contended. In some quarters, the view is strongly held that filth and intrigues characterise the institution these days. Judges are said to be comfortable in companies they never would have kept in the past. It is being insinuated that some judicial officers even campaign for politicians. It cannot be more damnifying.” ; said that some years ago “appointment to the bench was strictly on merit. Sound knowledge of the law, integrity, honour and hard work distinguished those who were elevated”, and continued: “Lobbying was unheard of. I never lobbied, not at any stage of my career, to secure any appointment or elevation. As much as possible, the most qualified men and women were appointed. That can no longer be said about appointments to the bench. The judiciary must be uniquely above board. Appointments should not be polluted by political, selfish and sectional interests. The place of merit, it must be urged, cannot be overemphasised. Public perceptions of the judiciary have over the years become witheringly scornful and monstrously critical”, and called for urgent reform in the judiciary to correct the alleged anomalies.

a925.speaker: Aletta Eises, Director of Education for the Oshikoto Region
a925.name: Aletta Eises
a925.title: Director of Education for the Oshikoto Region
a925.speech: Accused the board of Oshigambo Secondary School of playing with children's education and of making announcements on social media without the knowledge of the responsible authorities.

a925.speaker: Simon Iitula, Chairperson of the Oshigambo Secondary School Board
a925.name: Simon Iitula
a925.title: Chairperson of the Oshigambo Secondary School Board
a925.speech: Informed parents on Saturday that they should not bring their children to school, since the school could not begin the second semester as planned because of Eises' refusal to release the subsidy funds ; Told parents that if they had questions about the opening of the school they should turn to Eises, and that should the director's office not respond to this urgent appeal, the school would take legal steps, including a possible lawsuit against Eises.

a925.speaker: Simon Iitula, Chairperson of the Oshigambo Secondary School Board
a925.name: Simon Iitula
a925.title: Chairperson of the Oshigambo Secondary School Board
a925.speech: Explained that the school administration was ready to receive the pupils again as soon as the necessary funds for food and other essential needs had been made available.

a925.speaker: Oshigambo Secondary School (letter to parents)
a925.name: Oshigambo Secondary School (letter to parents)
a925.speech: On Sunday morning the school published another letter informing parents that the pupils could return to school, as the dispute had now been settled.

a925.speaker: Simon Iitula, Chairperson of the Oshigambo Secondary School Board (letter)
a925.name: Simon Iitula
a925.title: Chairperson of the Oshigambo Secondary School Board (letter)
a925.speech: Expressed to the office of Permanent Secretary Sanet Steenkamp his “heartfelt thanks for the swift and effective intervention to resolve the problem”; said Steenkamp's commitment had been decisive in finding a timely solution and in ensuring that the pupils could return to a safe learning environment.

a925.speaker: Aletta Eises, Director of Education for the Oshikoto Region
a925.name: Aletta Eises
a925.title: Director of Education for the Oshikoto Region
a925.speech: Said in a telephone interview that she had not been informed that the school had issued a letter instructing parents not to bring the pupils back for the second semester; referred the questions to the school board and said it had issued its letter without consulting the ministry or the director's office; asked whether the funds had been transferred to the school account, said: “They must check their accounts.”

a993.speaker: US congressman (unnamed)
a993.name: US congressman (unnamed)
a993.speech: Said that USAID was financing terrorism in Africa.

a993.speaker: Sergey Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister
a993.name: Sergey Lavrov
a993.title: Russian Foreign Minister
a993.speech: Announced that Russia will open seven new embassies in Africa.

a1344.speaker: Idrissou Mora-Kpai, film director
a1344.name: Idrissou Mora-Kpai
a1344.title: film director
a1344.speech: For the man for whom cinema has always been "a journey towards the unknown, towards a new experience, with a different sense of time", "America Street" is an opportunity to evoke in such a realistic way the human condition in a two-speed society, and also an opportunity to draw the attention of Black leaders in general to their responsibility in transforming their societies.

a1488.speaker: Representatives of Niger’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and K. Samba, head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP) office
a1488.name: Representatives of Niger’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and K. Samba
a1488.title: head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP) office
a1488.speech: Thanked Russia for its contribution to the world organisation’s activities in the country, and stressed that thanks to Russian aid it is possible to meet three months’ worth of sunflower oil consumption needs for groups in need, including refugees.

a1488.speaker: Russia (statement)
a1488.name: Russia (statement)
a1488.speech: For its part, Russia will continue to provide the necessary humanitarian support to the people of the friendly Republic of Niger.

a1498.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli Defence Minister
a1498.name: Israel Katz
a1498.title: Israeli Defence Minister
a1498.speech: issued a statement, saying he has ordered the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) to "respond forcefully to Iran's violation of the ceasefire with intense strikes against regime targets in the heart of Tehran".

a1498.speaker: Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister
a1498.name: Abbas Araghchi
a1498.title: Iran's Foreign Minister
a1498.speech: said earlier that it would only stop its attacks if Israel did the same. ; Araghchi had said Iran would halt its military response if Israel stopped its strikes on Iran by that time.

a1498.speaker: Medics in southern Israel
a1498.name: Medics in southern Israel
a1498.speech: say five people were killed in Beer Sheba overnight.

a1498.speaker: Israeli government / Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office
a1498.name: Israeli government / Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office
a1498.speech: said it had agreed to Donald Trump's ceasefire proposal, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office saying Israel would respond "forcefully" to any violations of the ceasefire with Iran. The statement added that Israel has achieved its goal of removing Iran's nuclear and ballistic threat and thanks Donald Trump and the US for their support in doing so.

a1498.speaker: Senior White House official (anonymous)
a1498.name: Senior White House official (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said that while Trump communicated directly with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, vice-president JD Vance, secretary of state and national security advisor Marco Rubio and Mideast envoy Steve Witkoff worked on the Iranians through direct and indirect channels ; said Israel agreed to the ceasefire deal on the condition that Iran stop its attacks, and that Iran agreed to those terms ; said Trump thanked the Qatari Emir for his help in mediating and asked the Emir to help persuade the Iranians to accept the deal.

a1498.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (Truth Social post)
a1498.name: Donald Trump
a1498.title: US President (Truth Social post)
a1498.speech: announced on his Truth Social platform that a deal had been struck, heralding a "complete and Total CEASEFIRE" between the warring nations that would lead to "an Official END to THE 12 DAY WAR." ; "Israel & Iran came to me, almost simultaneously, and said, "PEACE!" I knew the time was NOW. The World, and the Middle East, are the real WINNERS! Both Nations will see tremendous LOVE, PEACE, AND PROSPERITY in their futures."

a1498.speaker: Two sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1498.name: Two sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said Trump told the Qatari Emir that the US was able to get Israel to agree to a ceasefire with Iran.

a1498.speaker: One source and a diplomat familiar with negotiations (anonymous)
a1498.name: One source and a diplomat familiar with negotiations (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said Vance coordinated with the office of Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani on details, and that after speaking with Al-Thani the Iranians agreed to the ceasefire proposal.

a1498.speaker: US official (anonymous)
a1498.name: US official (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said that a series of calls with the Qatari Emir was pivotal on the Iranian side.

a1498.speaker: Iranian state media
a1498.name: Iranian state media
a1498.speech: announced Tuesday local time that a ceasefire has been "imposed on the enemy" after the country's military response to "US aggression."

a1498.speaker: Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister (post on X)
a1498.name: Abbas Araghchi
a1498.title: Iran's Foreign Minister (post on X)
a1498.speech: thanked his country's armed forces and said military operations against Israel "continued until the very last minute," hinting that hostilities may have ended. "The military operations of our powerful Armed Forces to punish Israel for its aggression continued until the very last minute, at 4 a.m."

a1498.speaker: Israeli military
a1498.name: Israeli military
a1498.speech: said it had identified missiles launched toward Israel from Iran and said its defensive systems were activated.

a1498.speaker: The White House
a1498.name: The White House
a1498.speech: maintains that the ceasefire deal was only possible due to the US strikes on three of Iran's nuclear facilities on Saturday.

a1498.speaker: Two sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1498.name: Two sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said Iranian officials had given Qatar advance notice of the retaliatory attack on the US military base in Qatar.

a1498.speaker: Diplomatic sources (anonymous, to CNN)
a1498.name: Diplomatic sources (anonymous
a1498.title: to CNN)
a1498.speech: told CNN they were hopeful that Iran's retaliatory strikes would serve as an off-ramp for Tehran to return to negotiations.

a1498.speaker: Regional source (anonymous)
a1498.name: Regional source (anonymous)
a1498.speech: confirmed there was an active effort underway to have Trump and the Iranian president meet in Turkey last week, but that it did not materialise.

a1498.speaker: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1498.name: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said Iran's consistent reply was that it was amenable to talks, but only if Israel suspended its military operations, and that even after the US strikes the Iranian foreign minister conveyed to some interlocutors a willingness to return to the table if Israel stops its military attacks on Iran. ; Said the Trump administration messaged Iran through intermediaries ahead of its strikes, with a twofold message: forthcoming US strikes would be contained, but also that the US terms for a diplomatic deal were clear and simple: no uranium enrichment.

a1498.speaker: Iran (government position, stated repeatedly)
a1498.name: Iran (government position
a1498.title: stated repeatedly)
a1498.speech: has repeatedly said that it retains the right to enrich uranium.

a1498.speaker: Source familiar with a secret meeting on Saturday (anonymous)
a1498.name: Source familiar with a secret meeting on Saturday (anonymous)
a1498.speech: said an intermediary reiterated to the Iranians that the White House was still willing to come to the table with no other conditions beyond enrichment.

a1498.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1498.name: Marco Rubio
a1498.title: US Secretary of State
a1498.speech: repeatedly publicly messaged a desire for direct negotiations with Iran on Sunday. He noted that a deal that allowed Tehran to have a civil nuclear program – without its own enrichment – was still on the table. "If they call right now and say we want to meet, let's talk about this, we're prepared to do that," the top US diplomat said on CBS 'Face the Nation'.

a1693.speaker: Institute for Security Studies (ISS) (research study)
a1693.name: Institute for Security Studies (ISS) (research study)
a1693.speech: Research by the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) indicated today that the suspension of the activities of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) could increase the risk of human rights violations, particularly in Mozambique.

a1703.speaker: USAID (statement on its website)
a1703.name: USAID (statement on its website)
a1703.speech: Said on Tuesday that all direct hire personnel would be put on leave from Friday, apart from "designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs"; said USAID personnel posted overseas will be recalled from their postings within 30 days; said it would consider case-by-case exceptions and extensions based on "personal or family hardship, mobility or safety concerns, or other reasons" ; "For example, the Agency will consider exceptions based on the timing of dependents' school term, personal or familial medical needs, pregnancy, and other reasons. Further guidance on how to request an exception will be forthcoming," the statement said ; "Thank you for your service."

a1703.speaker: Congressional Research Service
a1703.name: Congressional Research Service
a1703.speech: According to the Congressional Research Service, USAID employs more than 10,000 people, about two-thirds of whom are stationed overseas.

a1703.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1703.name: Donald Trump
a1703.title: US President
a1703.speech: Asked by a reporter on Tuesday if he was preparing to "wind down" the agency, Trump said, "I think so."

a1703.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1703.name: Marco Rubio
a1703.title: US Secretary of State
a1703.speech: On Monday confirmed that he was serving as acting administrator of USAID.

a1703.speaker: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1703.name: Elon Musk
a1703.title: CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1703.speech: Has called USAID a "criminal organisation", without substantiation, and claimed the agency is a "viper's nest of radical-left Marxists who hate America".

a1766.speaker: President of Ghana
a1766.name: President of Ghana
a1766.speech: Is particularly concerned about the potential $78.2 million shortfall, which will have a detrimental effect on critical interventions, including malaria prevention, maternal and child health, family planning, reproductive health, nutrition, and the fight against HIV/AIDS.

a1766.speaker: Stephen Agbenyo, Ph.D., Executive Director, Savana Signatures (author)
a1766.name: Stephen Agbenyo
a1766.title: Ph.D., Executive Director, Savana Signatures (author)
a1766.speech: Argues that Ghana's excessive dependence on external aid has been exposed by the suspension of USAID funding, which has underscored the pressing necessity for sustainable domestic financing ; that Ghana can achieve sustainable development by diversifying funding sources, empowering local industries, and developing robust domestic policies, thereby reducing its reliance on foreign aid ; and that the crisis serves as a significant wake-up call for the NGO sector to explore alternative methods of resource mobilisation and diversify its funding sources.

a1931.speaker: Humanitarian community in Somalia, led by George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.name: Humanitarian community in Somalia
a1931.title: led by George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.speech: Has called on all parties to protect civilians and humanitarian workers in areas of conflict.

a1931.speaker: George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.name: George Conway
a1931.title: Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.speech: "The World Humanitarian Day theme for this year, #ActForHumanity, urges the world to do a better job of protecting civilians and humanitarians, especially in conflict zones." ; "It implores us to reflect and honour aid workers, who around the world, are targeted or obstructed as they work to help people in need."

a1931.speaker: George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.name: George Conway
a1931.title: Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.speech: "On this day, every year, we shine a spotlight on humanitarian workers and the millions of civilians around the world whose lives have been caught up in humanitarian crises." ; "I pay particular tribute to Somali aid workers who, despite immense challenges, have demonstrated their commitment to serve those in most need of assistance and protection."

a1931.speaker: George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.name: George Conway
a1931.title: Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a1931.speech: "Authorities and non-state armed groups have clear and long-established international legal obligations in conflict, including to protect civilians from harm, spare schools and hospitals and ensure the safe passage of humanitarian workers." ; "Every time these rules are broken, human suffering intensifies and civilians are pushed into greater despair. Every time these lines are crossed, humanitarian needs grow."

a2085.speaker: Statutory Instrument 87 of 2025, Government of Zimbabwe (gazetted)
a2085.name: Statutory Instrument 87 of 2025
a2085.title: Government of Zimbabwe (gazetted)
a2085.speech: According to Statutory Instrument 87 of 2025 gazetted last Friday, only contractors will be allowed to import in cases of necessity, while all processors will be required to increase... (banning the importation of oilseeds, grain and related products in a bid to promote local production and reduce the country's ballooning import bill).

a2170.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a2170.name: United Nations (UN)
a2170.speech: has said the ongoing drought will be crossing the famine phase this month.

a2170.speaker: Joint report by the World Bank and FAO (2018)
a2170.name: Joint report by the World Bank and FAO (2018)
a2170.speech: According to the report, the share of crops to GDP in Somalia has dropped by 8 percentage points from the prewar period to stand at 10%.

a2170.speaker: FAO
a2170.name: FAO
a2170.speech: indicating that less than 20% of the irrigated farms are being utilized.

a2170.speaker: World Bank and FAO
a2170.name: World Bank and FAO
a2170.speech: have warned that river flows especially to Shabelle river could be cut by 80% should Ethiopia fully implement its water masterplan.

a2170.speaker: National Development Plan for 2020-2024 (NDP-9)
a2170.name: National Development Plan for 2020-2024 (NDP-9)
a2170.speech: sets agriculture under pillar three and envisages sustainable interventions to cushion farmers from adverse weather patterns, creation of new markets and revising administrative procedures to spur growth in the sector.

a2170.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a2170.name: United Nations (UN)
a2170.speech: estimates that Somalia can produce milk worth $3.3 billion annually.

a2170.speaker: Report by One Earth Future
a2170.name: Report by One Earth Future
a2170.speech: foreign trawlers have illegally caught up to 2.4 million tons of fish in Somalia in the last 60 years.

a2170.speaker: World Bank Somali Economic Update for 2021
a2170.name: World Bank Somali Economic Update for 2021
a2170.speech: estimates that the cost of imported food products in 2020 stood at $1.2 billion amounting to 31% of total imports.

a2200.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a2200.name: Antonio Guterres
a2200.title: UN Secretary-General
a2200.speech: Urged the world to "rev up the engine of development" at an aid conference in Spain ; told delegates at the opening of the conference that two-thirds of United Nations sustainable development goals set for 2030 were "lagging" and more than $4.0 trillion of annual investment would be needed to achieve them ; said the crisis meant children going unvaccinated, girls dropping out of school and families suffering hunger ; urged the international community to "change course" and "repair and rev up the engine of development to accelerate investment" in "a world shaken by inequalities, climate chaos and raging conflicts".

a2200.speaker: Oxfam (international charity)
a2200.name: Oxfam (international charity)
a2200.speech: Says the cuts to development aid are the largest since 1960.

a2200.speaker: World Bank
a2200.name: World Bank
a2200.speech: More than 800 million people live on less than $3.0 a day, according to the World Bank, with rising extreme poverty affecting sub-Saharan Africa in particular.

a2200.speaker: UN data
a2200.name: UN data
a2200.speech: The total external debt of the group of least developed countries has more than tripled in 15 years, according to UN data.

a2200.speaker: Common declaration to be adopted in Seville (the "Seville Commitment" document)
a2200.name: Common declaration to be adopted in Seville (the "Seville Commitment" document)
a2200.speech: The document reaffirms commitment to the UN development goals such as eliminating poverty and hunger, promoting gender equality, reforming tax systems and international financial institutions. The text also calls on development banks to triple their lending capacity, urges lenders to ensure predictable finance for essential social spending and for more cooperation against tax evasion.

a2200.speaker: Ilan Henzler, 28, protester
a2200.name: Ilan Henzler
a2200.title: 28, protester
a2200.speech: "Global South countries will never be able to decide how they want to do development if they are bound to the new colonial debt," protester Ilan Henzler, 28, told AFP.

a2358.speaker: tradingeconomics.com (data cited)
a2358.name: tradingeconomics.com (data cited)
a2358.speech: Puts Namibia debt to GDP at 69.60% in 2020.

a2714.speaker: Stanislas Touobekoure Meda, Director General of Quarries
a2714.name: Stanislas Touobekoure Meda
a2714.title: Director General of Quarries
a2714.speech: said that despite its geological potential characterised by abundant quarry substances, Burkina Faso remains a large importer of construction materials, and that it is time to reverse the situation by making the quarry sector a lever of sustainable development and industrial sovereignty. "And that requires adapting technologies to the specific features of local materials, strengthening the skills of actors for new production practices, drawing up clear and incentivising regulatory frameworks, and mobilising stakeholders around a common and inclusive strategy." ; added that there is the opportunity to strengthen research and innovation in order to position Burkina Faso as a regional reference actor in sustainable cement, and specified that the workshop aims to map the potential of the country's quarry substances, strengthen the technical and regulatory capacities of professionals, encourage the sharing of experiences, identify paths to sustainable industrialisation and propose public policy orientations.

a2714.speaker: Yacouba Zabre Gouba, Minister of Energy, Mines and Quarries
a2714.name: Yacouba Zabre Gouba
a2714.title: Minister of Energy, Mines and Quarries
a2714.speech: said the choice of the theme of this Pre-SAMAO reflects the political will of the government to develop the national cement industry. "Burkina Faso, like many other African countries, is experiencing sustained urban growth, accompanied by ever-increasing demand for infrastructure and housing, generating considerable needs for construction materials in general and cement in particular." ; "The cement industry, which is at the heart of construction, can become a powerful lever of transformation. Indeed, by incorporating alternative materials such as calcined clay, dolomitic limestone or lime, tuffs, basalt or granite powder, we have the opportunity to produce low-carbon cements, while stimulating the local economy and reducing our dependence on imports."

a2714.speaker: Yacouba Zabre Gouba, Minister of Energy, Mines and Quarries
a2714.name: Yacouba Zabre Gouba
a2714.title: Minister of Energy, Mines and Quarries
a2714.speech: invited the participants to hold open, constructive, action-oriented exchanges capable of guiding policies, in order to build together a Burkinabe cement industry that is a symbol of sustainability, innovation and national pride and that strengthens its industrial sovereignty.

a2714.speaker: Jacques Amiong, President of the Association of Cement Makers of Burkina and Director General of CIMBURKINA
a2714.name: Jacques Amiong
a2714.title: President of the Association of Cement Makers of Burkina and Director General of CIMBURKINA
a2714.speech: "Quarry activity involves many participants, among them cement makers. For cement makers, quarry substances are very important elements that go into cement manufacturing. It is therefore an honour for us to be at this workshop, which gives us the chance to take part in developing research relating to improving the environmental conditions of the cement industry." ; noted that the workshop will serve as a platform to review the challenges linked to developing local materials, to question environmental protection practices and cement production, and to highlight the roles of all the stakeholders, notably the public authorities, the cement makers and quarry professionals.

a2937.speaker: Observatory of Trade, Industry and Services (Ocis) of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (Cci-Benin)
a2937.name: Observatory of Trade
a2937.title: Industry and Services (Ocis) of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (Cci-Benin)
a2937.speech: According to Ocis, the economic situation remains broadly favourable thanks to price stability and the resilience of several productive sectors.

a2937.speaker: Benin Agency for the Promotion of Investment and Exports (Apiex) (figures)
a2937.name: Benin Agency for the Promotion of Investment and Exports (Apiex) (figures)
a2937.speech: According to Apiex figures, 14,863 businesses were registered in Benin between April and June 2025, a 2 per cent decline compared with the first quarter, when 15,166 new entities were recorded; sole proprietorships account for 89 per cent of creations against 11 per cent for companies, women head 37 per cent of new entities and young entrepreneurs aged 21 to 45 account for 86 per cent of registrations.

a2937.speaker: National Institute of Statistics and Demography (Instad) (data)
a2937.name: National Institute of Statistics and Demography (Instad) (data)
a2937.speech: According to Instad data, the annual average inflation rate came to 1.1 per cent at the end of June against 1.2 per cent in April, a decline of 8.33 per cent; over three months the general level of consumer prices rose by 0.4 per cent, driven by housing, water, electricity and fuel (+4.1 per cent), food products (+0.7 per cent) and energy products (+1.4 per cent), offset by falls in transport (-1.9 per cent), alcoholic beverages (-0.7 per cent) and financial services (-0.7 per cent).

a2937.speaker: OCIS report, July 2025 (based on APIEx data, Monentreprise.bj)
a2937.name: OCIS report
a2937.title: July 2025 (based on APIEx data, Monentreprise.bj)
a2937.speech: Cited as the source of the key figures on the evolution of business registrations in the second quarter of 2025.

a2984.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a2984.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a2984.speech: Projects South Sudan's economy is poised for significant growth, with a 4.0 per cent increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) expected in 2025, hinging on rising oil exports and subsiding security challenges; the AfDB's forecast is even more robust for 2026, anticipating a substantial GDP growth of 12.1 per cent, a projection that hinges critically on stability in neighbouring Sudan, which provides the vital pipeline for South Sudan's oil exports.

a2984.speaker: AfDB Country Focus Report 2025, "Making South Sudan's capital work for South Sudan's development"
a2984.name: AfDB Country Focus Report 2025
a2984.title: "Making South Sudan's capital work for South Sudan's development"
a2984.speech: The report highlights that a de-escalation of internal political tensions and the continued implementation of Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms will be crucial in spurring this growth. The report acknowledged that South Sudan's real GDP notably contracted by 27.6 per cent in 2023/2024, a sharp decline from a 2.5 per cent growth in 2022/2023. The AfDB report underscores that South Sudan's economy is one of the most resource-dependent economies on the continent: oil alone represents over 50 per cent of the GDP, accounts for about 80 per cent of exports, and contributes over 90 per cent of government revenues.

a2984.speaker: Hoth Tot Chany, Senior National Country Economist, African Development Bank
a2984.name: Hoth Tot Chany
a2984.title: Senior National Country Economist, African Development Bank
a2984.speech: "We projected that the output will be positive, after the announcement of resumption of oil in January, we had to revised our focus based on the available information, and as of now, we project that by the end of this fiscal year, the economy will grow by 4 percent." ; "But in the following year, if the production continues without any interruption, we project that the economy will grow by 12.1 per cent because of oil coming and stability in other areas to support agricultural production." ; According to Chany, to realize these projections and ensure sustainable development, the AfDB presented several key recommendations.

a3070.speaker: Julius Kanubah, President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.name: Julius Kanubah
a3070.title: President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.speech: “Mr. President, permit us to draw your attention to a few issues confronting the media community in Liberia and the country in general” ; “While we recognized that Liberia has made significant progress in respecting press freedom and free speech, the media remains severely challenged, both in terms of human and financial resources.” ; “Advertising revenues have significantly fallen, affecting the operations of media entities, the quality of journalism, and crucially the welfare and conditions of work of journalists and media workers, whose take home pay, if available, cannot take them home, in most instances.” ; Said the existing advertisers such as the government, in addition to reducing the level of advertising, remain hugely in debt to media entities, thereby undermining the operational capability and viability of the media to sustain the costs of production.

a3070.speaker: Julius Kanubah, President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.name: Julius Kanubah
a3070.title: President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.speech: Cited what he called the “near-total departure of USAID”, especially its media development interventions, which has created a very big vacuum, impacting the capacity building and institutional strengthening of the media across Liberia; expressed hope that the government could assume some of those shocks.

a3070.speaker: Julius Kanubah, President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.name: Julius Kanubah
a3070.title: President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.speech: “Mr. President, Community Radio Stations—vital sources of information in our counties—are increasingly facing interference from some County Superintendents. This undermines their independence and jeopardizes their ability to serve our communities effectively. We urge your administration to protect these broadcasters and uphold their right to operate free from political interference or influence.”

a3070.speaker: Julius Kanubah, President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.name: Julius Kanubah
a3070.title: President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.speech: Spoke of the need to transform the Liberia Broadcasting System (LBS) into a true public service broadcaster, calling on the LBS to epitomize accountability, serving not just the government’s interests but also the diverse voices of all Liberians, a shift he said is crucial for fostering an informed citizenry and enhancing democratic participation.

a3070.speaker: Julius Kanubah, President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.name: Julius Kanubah
a3070.title: President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.speech: Divulged his administration’s vision to restore and enhance the integrity and credibility of the institution of journalism and media, but indicated to President Boakai that it “requires a concerted effort, working with your administration in upholding press freedom and free speech and expression”.

a3070.speaker: Julius Kanubah, President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.name: Julius Kanubah
a3070.title: President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a3070.speech: Told President Boakai that “if there is anything your government must not compromise, it is the issue of the rule of law.” ; “Respect for and adherence to the rule of law is essentially critical to keeping the peace and enhancing the development of our country. Let’s respect the rule of law and let’s use the rule of law to fight corruption.”

a3161.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) reports
a3161.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) reports
a3161.speech: indicate that, in the 2023/2024 agricultural season, rainfall was drastically reduced, compromising the livelihoods of hundreds of thousands of rural families.

a3161.speaker: A farmer from the Panda region (unnamed)
a3161.name: A farmer from the Panda region (unnamed)
a3161.speech: "Before, even with the river right here beside us, the water passed us by without being used. In times without rain, the river would dry up, and we were left with nothing to irrigate the fields, to drink or for the animals. It was a very complicated situation." ; "Since they built the retention wall, the situation has improved a lot. Now we manage to store the water and we can produce all year round. Before, we were afraid of the future, but now we have hope."

a3161.speaker: A woman farmer from Panda (unnamed)
a3161.name: A woman farmer from Panda (unnamed)
a3161.speech: "I decided to bet on cashew because I saw a producer from my area greatly improve his life with this crop. I received cashew seedlings and now I have a field full of hope. I know it is work that takes time, but I believe it will be my guarantee for the future. I want to be able to support my children and give them a better life."

a3161.speaker: Belem Monteiro, Vice-President of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD) of Mozambique
a3161.name: Belem Monteiro
a3161.title: Vice-President of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD) of Mozambique
a3161.speech: stressed the importance of investing in sustainable solutions and in the autonomy of communities: "Our objective is to prevent populations from depending exclusively on external aid to survive. We have resources in the country that can be used efficiently. Here in Panda, we have seen clear examples that, with small investments, it is possible to change lives. The construction of the barrier on the Inhassune river and the introduction of drought-tolerant crops are just a few examples." ; "Today, the people of Panda have concrete examples that it is possible to face climate change in a more autonomous way. We are working to expand these initiatives to other regions and thus guarantee food security and greater income for the affected families."

a3161.speaker: Belem Monteiro, Vice-President of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD) of Mozambique
a3161.name: Belem Monteiro
a3161.title: Vice-President of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD) of Mozambique
a3161.speech: underlined that the anticipatory actions implemented in the district minimised the impacts of El Nino which, although severe, did not reach the critical levels initially feared, and reinforced that the way forward must include strategic planning that involves the communities, invests in resilient infrastructure and ensures the diversification of economic activities.

a3179.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3179.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3179.speech: Has stated that Nigeria and other sub-Saharan African countries are paying more to borrow at home than abroad as they turn increasingly to domestic banks to plug financing gaps, deepening risks for lenders and squeezing private investment ; Warned that new domestic public borrowing is "significantly more expensive than external borrowing" in many countries, adding that heavy reliance on banks is raising funding costs further and "crowding out private-sector investment."

a3179.speaker: Abebe Aemro Selassie, Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.name: Abebe Aemro Selassie
a3179.title: Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.speech: "The domestic cost of capital remains elevated across the region. Local financial markets are underdeveloped - characterised by shallow depth, fragmentation, illiquidity and high transaction costs and lending spreads." ; Said domestic bank holdings of sovereign debt are "large and growing faster in sub-Saharan Africa than in the rest of the world," creating a "vicious potential feedback loop" in which weakening government finances threaten banks' soundness, curbing credit and heightening fiscal stress.

a3179.speaker: Abebe Aemro Selassie, Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.name: Abebe Aemro Selassie
a3179.title: Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.speech: "Six months ago, our assessment highlighted the region's strong policy efforts and that growth had exceeded expectations in 2024. But, we also noted a sudden realignment of global priorities and increasingly turbulent external conditions - marked by weaker demand, softer commodity prices, and tighter financial markets. Today, these global headwinds continue to test the region's recovery and resilience. Sub-Saharan Africa's economic growth is projected to hold steady at 4.1 percent in 2025, with a modest pickup expected in 2026. This reflects ongoing progress in macroeconomic stabilisation and reform efforts across key economies. Several countries - Benin, Cote d'Ivoire, Ethiopia, Rwanda, and Uganda - are among the world's fastest-growing. However, resource-intensive, and conflict-affected countries continue to face significant challenges, with only modest gains in income per capita".

a3179.speaker: Abebe Aemro Selassie, Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.name: Abebe Aemro Selassie
a3179.title: Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.speech: Noted that the external environment remains challenging: "Global growth is slowing, and commodity prices are diverging. Oil prices are declining, while prices for cocoa, coffee, copper, and gold remain elevated. External financing terms have improved somewhat, allowing a few countries, notably Kenya and Angola most recently, to access international capital markets. The global trade policy and aid landscape has also deteriorated. Tariffs on exports to the United States have increased, and preferential access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act has expired. While the direct exposure is relatively modest for most countries in the region, broader trade policy uncertainty is weighing on growth. The projected sharp decline in foreign aid leaves several lower-income and fragile economies particularly exposed. Affected governments have sought to reallocate budgetary resources but with limited fiscal space, they have limited room for maneuver".

a3179.speaker: Abebe Aemro Selassie, Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.name: Abebe Aemro Selassie
a3179.title: Director of the African Department at the IMF
a3179.speech: "It is encouraging to see the region showing remarkable resilience. Although this will continue to be tested in the coming months. Pressure points include rising debt service costs, which are crowding out development spending; a shift toward domestic financing that is deepening the sovereign-bank nexus; inflation that has eased at the regional level but remains in double digits in about one-fifth of the region, and external buffers that are under pressure and need to be rebuilt".

a3179.speaker: Abebe Aemro Selassie, Director of the African Department at the IMF, citing the IMF October 2025 Regional Economic Outlook report
a3179.name: Abebe Aemro Selassie
a3179.title: Director of the African Department at the IMF, citing the IMF October 2025 Regional Economic Outlook report
a3179.speech: "Our October 2025 Regional Economic report is significant potential for countries in the region to raise revenues through comprehensive tax policy reforms and improved tax administration. This includes modernising tax systems through digitalisation, streamlining inefficient tax expenditures, and strengthening enforcement via targeted compliance strategies. However, these efforts must go beyond technical adjustments."

a3476.speaker: World Bank (diagnostic trade integration studies)
a3476.name: World Bank (diagnostic trade integration studies)
a3476.speech: Diagnostic studies of trade integration conducted by the World Bank find inadequacies in transport, communications, and energy infrastructure - roads, ports, airports, telecommunications, electric power, and so on.

a3476.speaker: China (government)
a3476.name: China (government)
a3476.speech: Has repeatedly emphasised its desire to engage with Africa in ways that advance the economic development of African countries.

a3599.speaker: Local media analysts interviewed for this project in January 2024 and March 2025 (anonymous)
a3599.name: Local media analysts interviewed for this project in January 2024 and March 2025 (anonymous)
a3599.speech: reported that NBT programming adheres closely to government messaging. Journalists operate under clearly defined mandates aligned with state policy, with little room for dissenting coverage.

a3599.speaker: Dragomir, M. (2025), State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC) (dataset/profile cited as source)
a3599.name: Dragomir
a3599.title: M. (2025), State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC) (dataset/profile cited as source)
a3599.speech: This article/profile is part of the State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, a continuously updated dataset published by the Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC).

a3700.speaker: Toyo Solar (Japanese solar panel manufacturer)
a3700.name: Toyo Solar (Japanese solar panel manufacturer)
a3700.speech: Announced that it is preparing to relocate its factory located in Vietnam to Ethiopia, and that it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Ethiopian Investment Commission last week to establish its first 2-gigawatt solar panel manufacturing plant in the Hawassa Industrial Park ; announced that it has allocated 60 million dollars (close to 7 billion birr) to build the factory and that this will be covered by advance payment from its own internal resources ; announced that it will begin installing production facilities in Hidar 2017 E.C. and will commission the factory and begin producing solar panels in the final quarter, and that its entry into Ethiopia will create job opportunities for up to 880 workers trained in manufacturing and engineering.

a3700.speaker: Toyo Solar (Japanese solar panel manufacturer)
a3700.name: Toyo Solar (Japanese solar panel manufacturer)
a3700.speech: Said that Ethiopia is strategic for Toyo's business expansion and announced that it chose the country because it enjoys duty-free market access granted by the US government ; citing that Ethiopia obtained a tariff exemption for bifacial solar cells under Section 201 of the US trade law of 1974, it further announced that it chose Ethiopia because the country has a favourable investment policy and is rich in hydropower resources.

a3700.speaker: Junsei Ryu, Chief Executive Officer of Toyo
a3700.name: Junsei Ryu
a3700.title: Chief Executive Officer of Toyo
a3700.speech: “Our decision to establish this manufacturing plant in Ethiopia is a key step in our strategic vision to diversify our supply chain and to increase our capacity to manufacture solar power products for the global market. Approximately 90 percent of Ethiopia's electricity generation comes from hydropower, while wind power accounts for 8 percent and the remaining 2 percent is obtained from geothermal power.” ; “The planned factory in Ethiopia will increase our production capacity and effectiveness and reduce costs. It will also enable us to respond quickly to market demands. As a result, it will make our company, Toyo, competitive and a key player in the renewable energy sector.”

a3766.speaker: Nelson Ashipala, Communications Manager of Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR)
a3766.name: Nelson Ashipala
a3766.title: Communications Manager of Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR)
a3766.speech: Informed the nbc News crew during a fact-finding visit to the resorts that the majority of the resorts were built during the colonial era and are thus costly to upgrade and maintain, resulting in the company being inundated with complaints by visitors ; said resorts such as Onkoshi, Okaukuejo, Waterberg, Ai Ais, and Sossus Dune will all have a facelift before the peak season for tourists by June 2023.

a3766.speaker: Nelson Ashipala, Communications Manager of Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR)
a3766.name: Nelson Ashipala
a3766.title: Communications Manager of Namibia Wildlife Resorts (NWR)
a3766.speech: Urged visitors to approach resort managers if they detect any problems, and avoid social media platforms, to expedite a reaction to rectify such issues.

a3766.speaker: Coster Shakwa, Onkoshi Resort Manager
a3766.name: Coster Shakwa
a3766.title: Onkoshi Resort Manager
a3766.speech: Says that with the upgrades of the resort, he anticipates an influx of tourists and a surge in revenue.

a3766.speaker: Christopher Bugbee, frequent traveller to Namibia and U.S. citizen
a3766.name: Christopher Bugbee
a3766.title: frequent traveller to Namibia and U.S. citizen
a3766.speech: Expressed joy with the upgrades, saying it will restore Etosha National Park to its former glory days as a flagship tourist site.

a3914.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.speech: Is worried about the immediate suspension of funding for HIV programmes in developing countries: "A halt to the funding of HIV programmes could immediately expose people living with HIV to an increased risk of illness and death, while undermining efforts to prevent transmission in communities and countries" ; "Such measures, if prolonged, could lead to an increase in new infections and deaths, reversing decades of progress and risking taking the world back to the 1980s and 1990s, when millions of people were dying of HIV every year around the world, including many people in the United States."

a3914.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.speech: Launches an appeal to the international community to correct course: "We call on the government of the United States to authorise additional exemptions to guarantee the provision of life-saving HIV treatment and care."

a3914.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.speech: States that during 2024, "PEPFAR and its partners, including WHO, worked on sustainability plans with countries for greater national ownership and a reduction of donor support through to 2030 and beyond. A sudden and prolonged halt to the programmes does not allow a managed transition and endangers the lives of millions of people."

a3914.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (public statement of Tuesday 28 January)
a3914.speech: "is committed to supporting PEPFAR and other partners, as well as national governments, in managing change processes effectively so as to minimise the impact on people living with HIV."

a4036.speaker: Attorney General's Office of Mozambique (Procuradoria-Geral da Republica)
a4036.name: Attorney General's Office of Mozambique (Procuradoria-Geral da Republica)
a4036.speech: Confirms that it was notified, through its lawyers, of the South African justice system's decision to extradite former Finance Minister Manuel Chang to the United States.

a4036.speaker: Source at the Attorney General's Office contacted by TVM (anonymous)
a4036.name: Source at the Attorney General's Office contacted by TVM (anonymous)
a4036.speech: Says the prosecution service is organising itself to comment on the matter in due course and on any steps to be taken.

a4036.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, President of Frelimo
a4036.name: Filipe Nyusi
a4036.title: President of Frelimo
a4036.speech: Thanks Vietnam for its support for Mozambique's candidacy as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council, and says that once elected Mozambique will give priority to dialogue in resolving any type of dispute between nations.

a4036.speaker: Survivors of the terrorist attack in Nanduli village, Ancuabe District
a4036.name: Survivors of the terrorist attack in Nanduli village
a4036.title: Ancuabe District
a4036.speech: Say they witnessed the burning of their homes, kidnappings and the dismemberment of people, among other atrocities.

a4049.speaker: Experts
a4049.name: Experts
a4049.speech: believe that the rollout of this drug could save hundreds of thousands of lives worldwide and represents a key step toward ending mother-to-child transmission of HIV in the region.

a4049.speaker: Jess Tesoriero, Public Affairs Officer at the US Embassy Maseru
a4049.name: Jess Tesoriero
a4049.title: Public Affairs Officer at the US Embassy Maseru
a4049.speech: told the Lesotho Times that Lesotho is now positioned to become one of the first countries globally to access lenacapavir through PEPFAR, marking a major milestone in the fight against HIV. "We are very pleased to announce that Lesotho will be among the first countries to be provided with lenacapavir by PEPFAR. We are working closely with the government of the Kingdom of Lesotho and providers to develop a rollout plan." ; said PEPFAR is prioritising countries based on the burden of HIV and the strength of their healthcare infrastructure to ensure effective distribution ; "This rollout will focus on prioritising distribution to pregnant and breastfeeding mothers — helping Lesotho move toward eliminating HIV infections in newborn children. We are excited to work with partners to help Lesotho on this exciting new PEPFAR initiative and on funding HIV/AIDS care and treatment services for all of Lesotho's 10 districts." ; emphasised that the initiative builds on "the very significant progress we have made together to reduce the number of new HIV/AIDS infections".

a4049.speaker: Daniel O'Day, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Gilead Sciences
a4049.name: Daniel O'Day
a4049.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Gilead Sciences
a4049.speech: "Lenacapavir is one of the most important scientific breakthroughs of our time and the result of nearly two decades of work by Gilead scientists. We are providing the medicine at no profit in this partnership so we can support the US government in delivering life-saving programmes where the need is most urgent."

a4049.speaker: Peter Sands, Executive Director of the Global Fund
a4049.name: Peter Sands
a4049.title: Executive Director of the Global Fund
a4049.speech: "Accelerating access to innovations like lenacapavir is imperative if we are to turn the tide against HIV. By targeting where lenacapavir can have the greatest effect, and working with the US and Gilead, we can help countries integrate it efficiently into their HIV prevention programmes — reducing new infections and enabling them to move more quickly along the pathway toward transition and self-reliance."

a4049.speaker: Jeremy Lewin, Senior Official for Foreign Assistance, Humanitarian Affairs, and Religious Freedom
a4049.name: Jeremy Lewin
a4049.title: Senior Official for Foreign Assistance, Humanitarian Affairs, and Religious Freedom
a4049.speech: "This US commitment exemplifies Secretary Rubio's America First life-saving assistance agenda: it champions American innovation, advances the Administration's goal of ending mother-to-child transmission of HIV, and will serve as an important catalyst for greater global and private sector investment in access to this groundbreaking medication."

a4049.speaker: 'Maneo Ntene, Principal Secretary in Lesotho's Ministry of Health
a4049.name: 'Maneo Ntene
a4049.title: Principal Secretary in Lesotho's Ministry of Health
a4049.speech: confirmed these developments, saying preparations were at an advanced stage and that the drug had already been ordered. "We as a country prefer youth to abstain from sex as a measure to prevent the spread of HIV, but now that we have failed in that aspect, we will administer lenacapavir."

a4049.speaker: Tarumbiswa Tapiwa, HIV and AIDS Programme Manager, Ministry of Health
a4049.name: Tarumbiswa Tapiwa
a4049.title: HIV and AIDS Programme Manager, Ministry of Health
a4049.speech: confirmed that the rollout is scheduled for February 2026, and said ongoing preparations include logistics, transportation, training of health workers, and the development of guidelines for proper administration. "We are still at a premature stage to say who the country will target as a pilot for this drug. There is still much to be done, including enacting guidelines and training health workers, among others."
