a4185.speaker: African Union (AU)
a4185.name: African Union (AU)
a4185.speech: has adopted President Akufo-Addo's proposal for mobile money interoperability across Africa. The reports — “Establishment of the African Union Financial Institutions (AUFIs)” and “Scaling up Interoperability for Economic Integration: Using Mobile Money to Buy and Sell Across Africa” — were endorsed by the AU, paving the way for implementation of mobile money interoperability across Africa.

a4185.speaker: GSMA
a4185.name: GSMA
a4185.speech: The total value of mobile money transactions was recently estimated to be over $1.26 trillion, according to GSMA, that is around 40% of Africa's GDP.

a4185.speaker: Nana Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana and AU Champion on Financial Institutions
a4185.name: Nana Akufo-Addo
a4185.title: President of Ghana and AU Champion on Financial Institutions
a4185.speech: emphasized the importance of mobile money interoperability, stating that while creating business opportunities and helping to tackle unemployment among the youth, continent wide interoperability will also make it easier for SMEs to conduct business and expand their reach.

a4185.speaker: African Union (AU)
a4185.name: African Union (AU)
a4185.speech: has called upon member states, regional economic communities, and relevant stakeholders to commit to achieving mobile money interoperability by 2027. This includes bringing all member states on board the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), allowing cross-border mobile money interoperability, and developing a continental regulatory framework for mobile money operations.

a4269.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4269.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4269.speech: Said on Monday that the Trump administration's decision to pause U.S. foreign aid has "substantially disrupted" supply of HIV treatments in eight countries, which could soon run out of these life-saving medicines ; The global health agency said that Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria and Ukraine could exhaust their supply of HIV treatments in the coming months.

a4269.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4269.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4269.speech: Said the WHO-coordinated Global Measles and Rubella Laboratory Network, with over 700 sites worldwide, also faces imminent shutdown.

a4269.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (separate statement)
a4269.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (separate statement)
a4269.speech: Said funding shortages could force 80% of WHO-supported essential health care services in Afghanistan to close; as of March 4, 167 health facilities had shut down due to funding shortages, and without urgent intervention, over 220 more facilities could close by June.

a4269.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4269.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4269.speech: Said on Monday that it plans to cut its funding target for emergency operations to $872 million from $1.2 billion in the 2026-2027 budget period.

a4269.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a4269.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a4269.title: WHO Director-General
a4269.speech: "The United States has a responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws direct funding for countries, it's done in an orderly and humane way that allows them to find alternative sources of funding," Ghebreyesus said on Monday.

a4495.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, International AIDS Society (IAS) President-Elect
a4495.name: Beatriz Grinsztejn
a4495.title: International AIDS Society (IAS) President-Elect
a4495.speech: Has called for sustained funding and resources support initiatives targeted to achieve global HIV targets, warning of donor fatigue, the rise of authoritarian governments and shrinking civil space ; "Crossing the last mile to end AIDS as a public health threat will require more attention and resources. International mechanisms such as PEPFAR and the Global Fund are under pressure. Now is not the time to question the value of these vital organisations," she said.

a4495.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, International AIDS Society (IAS) President-Elect
a4495.name: Beatriz Grinsztejn
a4495.title: International AIDS Society (IAS) President-Elect
a4495.speech: Addressing delegates at the closing ceremony of AIDS 2024, underscored the conference's theme: Put people first ; "As a lesbian from Latin America and the director of the first sexual and gender minorities' health clinic in Rio de Janeiro, I witness firsthand every day how we are still failing the most marginalized people. In Brazil, new HIV acquisitions are rising among young black men who have sex with men, illustrating the structural gender-related violence and racism fuelling the epidemic."

a4495.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, International AIDS Society (IAS) President-Elect
a4495.name: Beatriz Grinsztejn
a4495.title: International AIDS Society (IAS) President-Elect
a4495.speech: Citing scientific breakthroughs presented at AIDS 2024, she called for equitable rollout of groundbreaking prevention drugs: "The promise of long-acting injectables highlights the need to ensure access across the global South. For prevention to work, we need to ensure everyone, everywhere has access to the latest technologies."

a4495.speaker: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a4495.name: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a4495.speech: Welcomed Grinsztejn from Brazil as IAS President and Kenneth Ngure from Kenya as President-Elect, and expressed deep gratitude to Sharon Lewin from Australia who stepped down as IAS President and assumed her role as Immediate Past President; the IAS also announced newly elected members of its Governing Council.

a4529.speaker: MTN (South African telecommunications company)
a4529.name: MTN (South African telecommunications company)
a4529.speech: Confirmed the internet shutdown in Eswatini, stating that it had received a directive from the Eswatini Communications Commission.

a4529.speaker: Political opposition and civil society in Eswatini
a4529.name: Political opposition and civil society in Eswatini
a4529.speech: Called for a more robust intervention by SADC, a call that has been met with a deafening silence.

a4529.speaker: Pro-democracy activists in Eswatini
a4529.name: Pro-democracy activists in Eswatini
a4529.speech: Have vowed to intensify demonstrations until democratic reforms take place and all opposition parties are unbanned.

a4608.speaker: Judith-Ann Walker, Executive Director and Founding Member of the development Research and Project Centre (dRPC)
a4608.name: Judith-Ann Walker
a4608.title: Executive Director and Founding Member of the development Research and Project Centre (dRPC)
a4608.speech: Said the NGO Support Initiative reflects the organisation's long-standing commitment to strengthening Nigerian civil society; explained that dRPC has been supporting local organisations since the early 1990s, with a focus on nurturing, enabling, and building their capacity to thrive; said the current initiative was launched not only to provide financial support but also to ensure long-term growth through mentorship and peer learning. “Nurturing and enabling and strengthening Nigerian civil society organisations is our mission, it is what we believe in and it's what we do as our piece of work.”

a4608.speaker: Judith-Ann Walker, Executive Director and Founding Member of dRPC
a4608.name: Judith-Ann Walker
a4608.title: Executive Director and Founding Member of dRPC
a4608.speech: Noted that although the initial plan was to select 10 organisations, the quality of applications received led to an expansion of the first cohort to 17 NGOs, each receiving N5 million in funding along with capacity-building support; said the three-month intervention combines financial support with mentorship from experienced CSO leaders; urged participants to demonstrate the impact that small grants can have on their communities, stressing that continued support, including a second cohort in September, would depend on how well the current recipients utilise the opportunity.

a4608.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4608.name: Donald Trump
a4608.title: US President
a4608.speech: In January announced the suspension of foreign assistance channelled through USAID, a major donor to numerous development programmes in Nigeria and other parts of the world.

a4608.speaker: Stanley Ukpai, Director of Programmes at dRPC
a4608.name: Stanley Ukpai
a4608.title: Director of Programmes at dRPC
a4608.speech: Said the US government terminated 83 per cent of USAID programmes globally, resulting in the cancellation of over 5,200 contracts, many of which supported services related to HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria treatment; said that in Nigeria alone, more than 1,000 jobs were lost due to the funding cuts, significantly affecting development efforts across multiple sectors; said the NSI was created as a direct response to these widespread losses. “This is why the dRPC is responding to bridge these gaps and cushion the substantial disruptions across sectors such as health, education, and economic development.”

a4608.speaker: Obashina Ogunbiyi, NSI Assessor
a4608.name: Obashina Ogunbiyi
a4608.title: NSI Assessor
a4608.speech: Said the selection process for the grant followed a rigorous multi-stage review that prioritised capacity, gender inclusion, and impact; said dRPC received a total of 495 applications, from which 139 valid entries were shortlisted; explained that a five-member assessment panel made up of past grantees of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, anchored by dRPC through the PACFaH@Scale project, evaluated the shortlisted applications. “We used different criteria in coming up with these 17 successful applicants. These organisations must have at least 50 per cent of their management as females” ; “We also looked at their capacity to actualise what their proposals said, and the potential impact of those proposals on women and communities.” ; added that the assessors saw their role as a way of giving back to the civil society ecosystem that had once supported their own growth.

a4639.speaker: US State Department
a4639.name: US State Department
a4639.speech: Presented the mini-summit at the White House with five African heads of state as a "targeted" follow-up to the 17th US-Africa Business Summit held in Luanda, where more than 2.5 billion dollars in agreements were signed.

a4639.speaker: Documents cited by Reuters and the Washington Post
a4639.name: Documents cited by Reuters and the Washington Post
a4639.speech: According to these documents, Senegal, Mauritania, Gabon and Liberia appear on a list of 25 African countries facing possible US migration restrictions, transmitted to African foreign ministries in mid-June and justified by "reliability problems" with identity documents and "administrative fraud".

a4639.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a4639.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a4639.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a4639.speech: "The presence of these five states, all bordering the Atlantic, reflects the importance the United States places on control of coasts that are vital for maritime trade and rich in resources, in a region marked by Russian-Chinese competition." ; Believes that the establishment of Russian military bases, arms deliveries via Conakry and military agreements with Togo or Sao Tome and Principe deeply worry Washington and its NATO allies.

a4639.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a4639.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a4639.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a4639.speech: Said Senegal's posture of sovereignty - Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko's cancellation of a sports training camp in the United States after a visa refusal, and the priority given to a visit to Beijing - "cannot leave Washington indifferent".

a4639.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a4639.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a4639.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a4639.speech: Faced with Trump's unpredictability and a persistent asymmetry, recommends "better African coordination in order to carry more weight in negotiations".

a4731.speaker: Climate Prediction and Applications Center (ICPAC) of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a4731.name: Climate Prediction and Applications Center (ICPAC) of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a4731.speech: Said on Wednesday that rising temperatures are set to elevate heat stress levels in several countries in the Horn of Africa ; noted in its latest forecast that the heat stress would happen in at least six countries ; according to the ICPAC, the temperatures are expected to rise up to 38 degrees Celsius in some of the affected countries, with warmer-than-usual temperatures forecast for most parts of the Greater Horn of Africa region in the coming weeks.

a4731.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and IGAD
a4731.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and IGAD
a4731.speech: Noted that adverse weather events affect food security, with some 67 million people risking starvation in the Horn.

a4731.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
a4731.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
a4731.speech: Said up to 49 billion U.S. dollars is needed to assist 187 million people in need of humanitarian assistance globally.

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On the return of Donald Trump and US foreign policy: “The worst thing we could do to ourselves and to Cape Verdeans would be to suffer in anticipation, because there are things we can control and others we cannot. Should American foreign aid decrease as a result of President Trump's decisions, there will be nothing we can do to counter that reality. He was legitimately elected by the sovereign will of the American people... President Trump has been in power before and we witnessed what he did and did not do, which were, to a large extent, acts of marketing and media impact. America survived and now we face a new set of circumstances.” He considers Cape Verde a small country that does not take part in major trade disputes and could hardly be pressured over tariffs or trade balances, and sees “no reason for Cape Verde to be the target of any retaliation, of whatever nature.”

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On fear of deportations: “It is a natural human reaction to feel some fear, but it is precisely at that moment that the public authorities and political leaders must intervene to reassure the population” ; said a working team has already been established involving several ministries (Family, Infrastructure, Defence and Internal Administration) developing a contingency plan, so that “should a Cape Verdean be deported, he will be received with full dignity in his own country” ; on mass deportation: “I believe not... We already have a list of deportations coming from the previous administration, of Cape Verdeans who were in an irregular situation, but there is no news of new deportations.”

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On the NATO partnership: explained that a tailored partnership means Cape Verde has a wide margin of choice within a set of options, and that Cape Verde faces serious security challenges in the Atlantic, starting with maritime security ; “I can assure you, right now, that Cape Verde has no interest whatsoever in having military bases here and I take this interview as an opportunity to reassure Cape Verdeans that NATO has not expressed any interest in our accession” ; “Cape Verde will be a partner State and a partner State does not accede, it develops a partnership programme that will constitute an anchorage” ; “States do not have feelings, they have interests. It is in our interest to have a safe anchorage in cooperation with our Atlantic neighbours.”

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On Russia and non-alignment: “What I can assure you is that Cape Verde's intention to cooperate with its Atlantic neighbours, including NATO, predates the geopolitical phenomenon that is occurring in West Africa” ; contested the idea that NATO's interest in Cape Verde is growing ; “To speak today of non-alignment is a delusion, a mere dream” ; “Cape Verde is an aligned country. It is aligned with rules-based multilateralism, with the principles defended and adopted by the United Nations... Cape Verde is also aligned with the principle of the sovereignty of States... Cape Verde defends human rights.”

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On the new fisheries agreement with the European Union: denied having said the fish does not belong to Cape Verde, calling it “an unfortunate attempt to distort my words”, and explained the agreement covers exclusively highly migratory species ; “It is false to claim that the agreement does not benefit our fishing communities” ; noted the old agreement covered 71 vessels for only 2.1 million euros while the current one covers 56 boats with a direct counterpart of 3.9 million euros ; “Therefore, I do not consider the agreement to be harmful to Cape Verde. Nobody is ‘stealing’ our fish.”

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On Morocco: said fisheries is one of the topics on the agenda with Morocco, along with Royal Air Maroc, the blue economy and other more sensitive matters ; “Morocco is a strategic partner that we cannot neglect in the name of merely ideological divergences” ; said Cape Verde “will not violate the right of peoples to self-determination” and rejected the claim that it is leaving behind the Saharawi people: “Nothing could be more false.”

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On the Brussels visit and EU funding: “We closed the year 2024 with the largest financing package ever allocated to Cape Verde under the Global Gateway, totalling 319 million euros – and that figure may still increase” ; said the meeting also discussed Cape Verde's aspiration to obtain full mobility with the European Union.

a4906.speaker: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.name: Cape Verdean Minister of Foreign Affairs (interviewee)
a4906.speech: On ECOWAS: said the organisation faces a context of instability due to extremist movements in the Sahel and the rise of political models attractive to defenders of more authoritarian regimes, but “I am convinced that ECOWAS will find its way”, noting that a military intervention to restore constitutional order after the coups was considered but ultimately discarded.

a5140.speaker: Human rights organisations
a5140.name: Human rights organisations
a5140.speech: have described the climate in Tanzania ahead of the general election as “deepening repression.”

a5140.speaker: Godfrey Polepole, brother of Humphrey Polepole
a5140.name: Godfrey Polepole
a5140.title: brother of Humphrey Polepole
a5140.speech: confirmed the abduction to the BBC, stating that the family had filed a report with the police.

a5140.speaker: UN human rights experts
a5140.name: UN human rights experts
a5140.speech: According to UN human rights experts, more than 200 cases of enforced disappearance have been recorded in the country since 2019.

a5140.speaker: Legal and Human Rights Centre
a5140.name: Legal and Human Rights Centre
a5140.speech: documented approximately 100 cases of enforced disappearance between 2015 and February 2025.

a5140.speaker: Tanzania Investment and Special Economic Zones Authority (TISEZA)
a5140.name: Tanzania Investment and Special Economic Zones Authority (TISEZA)
a5140.speech: has announced that the regions of Dar es Salaam, Pwani, and Arusha have continued to lead in attracting new investment projects between July and September 2025.

a5140.speaker: Gilead Teri, TISEZA Director General
a5140.name: Gilead Teri
a5140.title: TISEZA Director General
a5140.speech: Speaking to journalists while presenting the authority’s first-quarter report, said the institution successfully registered 201 investment projects worth TSh 6.18 trillion, expected to create 20,800 jobs for Tanzanians and drive technological and economic growth nationwide.

a5140.speaker: Tundu Lissu, CHADEMA national chairperson
a5140.name: Tundu Lissu
a5140.title: CHADEMA national chairperson
a5140.speech: protested that police had barred his named supporters from entering the courtroom, including his brother, Dr Stephen Linco, who had travelled from Germany. He demanded to know who was in charge of the proceedings. “I want to know, is this a police court or a court of the United Republic of Tanzania?” Lissu asked the bench. “Who decides who enters, the police or the court? This is not a court-martial. The judges are superior.”

a5140.speaker: Major General Maychel Asmi, Deputy Head of the UN Peacekeeping Forces in CAR
a5140.name: Major General Maychel Asmi
a5140.title: Deputy Head of the UN Peacekeeping Forces in CAR
a5140.speech: In his address, commended TANBAT 08 for its leadership, discipline, and the remarkable camaraderie displayed throughout its operational tour.

a5140.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Theofil Nguruwe, commanding officer of TANBAT 08
a5140.name: Lieutenant Colonel Theofil Nguruwe
a5140.title: commanding officer of TANBAT 08
a5140.speech: stated that the honour was a testament to the loyalty, hard work, and patriotism of his troops in fulfilling their international duties.

a5279.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.name: Nicholas Haysom
a5279.title: UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.speech: Warned that South Sudan is edging dangerously close to full-scale conflict amid rising tensions between the country's rival leaders, and told the UN Security Council that the fragile peace between President Salva Kiir and former First Vice President Riek Machar has deteriorated into direct military confrontation: "This situation is darkly reminiscent of the conflicts of 2013 and 2016, which cost over 400,000 lives," urging the international community to help de-escalate tensions and preserve the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement ; "We need look no further than across the northern border to Sudan for a stark reminder of how quickly a country can descend into catastrophic conflict. This region cannot afford another crisis that could further destabilize an already fragile landscape." ; "The Revitalised Peace Agreement remains the only viable framework to break this cycle of violence in South Sudan."

a5279.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.name: Nicholas Haysom
a5279.title: UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.speech: Said misinformation, disinformation and hate speech are inflaming political and ethnic divisions, threatening to unravel years of fragile peacebuilding efforts.

a5279.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.name: Nicholas Haysom
a5279.title: UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.speech: Highlighted ongoing diplomatic efforts with the African Union, regional bloc IGAD, Pope Francis and others to restore dialogue and urge restraint, and called on the Security Council to support initiatives that promote respect for the ceasefire, ease tensions in hotspots such as the Nasir region of Upper Nile state, and ensure the release of detained officials; the parties, he emphasized, must recommit to dialogue, consensus-based decision-making, and nonviolence.

a5279.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.name: Nicholas Haysom
a5279.title: UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.speech: "UNMISS is a peacekeeping mission - not an army - and cannot be everywhere, all at once," Haysom noted, warning that the mission's ability to respond remains limited by access denials and operational constraints.

a5279.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.name: Nicholas Haysom
a5279.title: UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a5279.speech: Stressed that while humanitarian efforts continue, they cannot replace political will: "What is needed is urgent, sustained, and coordinated action from national leaders, regional guarantors and the international community. Another war is a risk South Sudan simply cannot afford - nor can the wider region."

a5279.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5279.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5279.speech: Described the political crisis as unfolding against a "humanitarian nightmare in the making."

a5279.speaker: Edem Wosornu, OCHA Director of Operations
a5279.name: Edem Wosornu
a5279.title: OCHA Director of Operations
a5279.speech: Told ambassadors that conditions have dramatically worsened over the past eight months, with over 9.3 million people - about three-quarters of the population - now requiring humanitarian assistance, nearly half of them children: "The humanitarian situation is deteriorating rapidly."

a5279.speaker: Aid agencies
a5279.name: Aid agencies
a5279.speech: Fear the crisis could worsen as the rainy season begins; last year floods displaced 1.4 million people, disrupted agriculture and triggered local violence - a scenario that could repeat itself in the coming months.

a5365.speaker: Professor Léonard Wantchékon, economist (researcher, IREEP study)
a5365.name: Professor Léonard Wantchékon
a5365.title: economist (researcher, IREEP study)
a5365.speech: "Money has strictly no (emphasis mine) effect on the vote, still less on electoral turnout" — an assertion made after conducting a "survey" of 150 villages during a single electoral cycle. In a similar survey conducted in 2001, the professor had reached the opposite conclusions.

a5365.speaker: Bally Sall, Senegalese moderator of the study's feedback session
a5365.name: Bally Sall
a5365.title: Senegalese moderator of the study's feedback session
a5365.speech: Says "the hypothesis according to which, in the African democratic game, the relationship between leaders and the people is based on political clientelism."

a5451.speaker: Vouanda Somé, health adviser at the Directorate of Prevention through Vaccination (Burkina Faso)
a5451.name: Vouanda Somé
a5451.title: health adviser at the Directorate of Prevention through Vaccination (Burkina Faso)
a5451.speech: Explained the transition: “From 15 August 2025, we are going to scale up malaria vaccination. That means that from that date, all 70 health districts in the country will vaccinate children against malaria.” ; said the choice of the R21 vaccine for the large-scale rollout is not due to a difference in efficacy with RTS,S, both being recognised by the WHO as safe and effective, and that the decision rests mainly on the greater availability and more advantageous cost of R21, making it more sustainable for a national vaccination programme ; “There is no question here of saying that one vaccine is more effective than the other. Both vaccines are effective and protect our children against malaria. The availability of the vaccines allows us to scale up. In terms of cost, we gain much more with R21 than with RTS,S.”

a5451.speaker: Vouanda Somé, health adviser at the Directorate of Prevention through Vaccination (Burkina Faso)
a5451.name: Vouanda Somé
a5451.title: health adviser at the Directorate of Prevention through Vaccination (Burkina Faso)
a5451.speech: Reassured: “The malaria vaccine, like the other vaccines we give our children, are safe and effective vaccines.” He adds that the progressive introduction of the vaccine since February 2024 has already made it possible to observe a reduction in cases in the areas concerned.

a5451.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5451.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5451.speech: Recognises both the RTS,S and R21 malaria vaccines as safe and effective.

a5451.speaker: Burkinabè health authorities
a5451.name: Burkinabè health authorities
a5451.speech: Recall that vaccination is only an additional tool and cannot replace existing prevention measures such as the use of insecticide-treated mosquito nets and environmental sanitation.

a5480.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia
a5480.name: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia
a5480.speech: Filed the proposal to the Development Assistance Group (DAG) early last week, stating that the funds will be used for three months to execute the emergency response plan the government drafted with the United Nations (UN).

a5480.speaker: COVID-19 Multi-Sectoral Preparedness & Response Plan (emergency response plan document)
a5480.name: COVID-19 Multi-Sectoral Preparedness & Response Plan (emergency response plan document)
a5480.speech: Indicates that an estimated 10 million people will require emergency assistance if the virus breaks out significantly in Ethiopia; the largest fund, 635 million dollars, will be used to serve food to 15 million people, 430 million dollars is required for health services for 39 million people, and 282 million dollars to provide shelter and non-food items for 2.5 million people; the government expects 102,000 confirmed cases in the coming three months; the agriculture sector is already under threat from the desert locust invasion affecting crop production in the Belg area; 24 million dollars was allocated to rescue the agriculture sector through more than 20 execution strategies.

a5480.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a5480.name: Eyob Tekalign (PhD)
a5480.title: State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a5480.speech: "The pandemic couldn't have come at a worse time - just as the country is undergoing major macroeconomic reform."

a5480.speaker: World Bank
a5480.name: World Bank
a5480.speech: Has estimated that, at a minimum, the economy will slow down significantly in the last quarter of the current fiscal year and remain slower than the pre-COVID-19 scenario in the next fiscal year with an expected recovery to commence in the second quarter of 2021.

a5480.speaker: Job Creation Commission
a5480.name: Job Creation Commission
a5480.speech: At a preliminary status, projects that in the next three months, 1.4 million jobs will be under threat.

a5480.speaker: Gro Intelligence (report)
a5480.name: Gro Intelligence (report)
a5480.speech: Approximately 18 million hectares or 84pc of cropland in Ethiopia is now affected by locusts, according to a report by Gro Intelligence, a company that provides data on agriculture; delays in the availability of agricultural inputs, fertiliser, pesticide and seeds will highly impact crop production and cultivation for the coming seasonal harvests, according to their data.

a5480.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a5480.name: Eyob Tekalign (PhD)
a5480.title: State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a5480.speech: "We have already mapped out every corner of the capital city in case things get dire in order to reach every community living in the city."

a5480.speaker: Macroeconomist (anonymous)
a5480.name: Macroeconomist (anonymous)
a5480.speech: Commented that the crisis will not be solved by the amount that has been requested for the emergency fund: "It may come to the point that the government needs more than this in the worst-case scenario." "The absence of remittances and exports is going to deteriorate the macroeconomic imbalance." The next most scary thing is how can the country get back on its feet after this, according to the expert, who adds that the government should start working on a recovery plan for after the crisis, and that this is the perfect time to capitalise on agriculture production by containing the desert locust invasion and focusing on making crop production more effective.

a5539.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5539.name: Donald Trump
a5539.title: US President
a5539.speech: Asserted on Monday that the preventive pardons granted by his predecessor Joe Biden to figures detested by the Republican president were not valid because, according to him, they were signed with an “autopen”; he wrote on his Truth Social platform overnight Sunday to Monday: “The ‘pardons’ that Sleepy Joe Biden granted to the unelected Committee of political thugs, and many others, are hereby declared VOID, VACANT, AND OF NO FURTHER FORCE OR EFFECT, because they were done by autopen.”

a5539.speaker: Joe Biden, former US President
a5539.name: Joe Biden
a5539.title: former US President
a5539.speech: A few hours before handing over power, on 20 January, had granted a series of preventive pardons to elected officials and civil servants in order to protect them from “unjustified and politically motivated judicial prosecutions”.

a5545.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a5545.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a5545.title: President of Djibouti
a5545.speech: Recalled that the implementation of the Djibouti Agenda 2035 must remain "the principal priority" of his government.

a5545.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a5545.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a5545.title: President of Djibouti
a5545.speech: Set out as another priority "the acceleration of public finance reforms" and the mobilisation of domestic resources.

a5545.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a5545.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a5545.title: President of Djibouti
a5545.speech: Highlighted the modernisation of port and road infrastructure, meant to strengthen Djibouti's attractiveness as a regional hub.

a5545.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a5545.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a5545.title: President of Djibouti
a5545.speech: Repeated the leitmotif of "youth at the centre of policies."

a5545.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a5545.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a5545.title: President of Djibouti
a5545.speech: Congratulated himself on the "response crowned with success" to the drought that affected the region.

a5545.speaker: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a5545.name: Ismaïl Omar Guelleh
a5545.title: President of Djibouti
a5545.speech: Expressed satisfaction at Djibouti's election to the presidency of the African Union Commission.

a5599.speaker: Brava island hospital
a5599.name: Brava island hospital
a5599.speech: Informed the population that between 4 and 7 November a medical team from the United States of America will be on the island to carry out consultations in various specialties such as General Medicine, Cardiology and Ophthalmology, and that those interested should go to the hospital secretariat to book appointments ; according to the same source, the initiative aims to strengthen the population's access to specialised health care and provide "more comprehensive" medical follow-up to the people of Brava.

a5681.speaker: Many Afghans
a5681.name: Many Afghans
a5681.speech: Say they are glad the foreign forces that prompted the Taliban insurgency left after a brutal 20-year war.

a5681.speaker: Zalmai, a resident of Kabul
a5681.name: Zalmai
a5681.title: a resident of Kabul
a5681.speech: “So many mujhahideen have been wounded (over the years), so many children became orphans and so many women become widows.”

a5681.speaker: Afghan government (statement)
a5681.name: Afghan government (statement)
a5681.speech: In a separate statement, the government said the day marked “the country's freedom from American occupation”.

a5681.speaker: Taliban fighters gathered at Massoud Square
a5681.name: Taliban fighters gathered at Massoud Square
a5681.speech: “Death to America! Death to occupation! Long live freedom!” chanted the fighters.

a5681.speaker: Shah Ahmad Omari, Taliban fighter
a5681.name: Shah Ahmad Omari
a5681.title: Taliban fighter
a5681.speech: Told AFP (remarks on the anniversary of the US withdrawal).

a5681.speaker: US military
a5681.name: US military
a5681.speech: “The burden of the war in Afghanistan, however, went beyond Americans,” the US military said on Tuesday.

a5681.speaker: Taliban social media accounts
a5681.name: Taliban social media accounts
a5681.speech: Posted videos and pictures of newly trained troops - many flaunting equipment the US military left behind ; “This is how you troll a superpower after humiliating them and forcing them to withdraw from your country,” read a tweet with a photo of a giant Taliban flag now painted on the wall of the former US embassy.

a5681.speaker: Marwa Naseem, female Kabul resident
a5681.name: Marwa Naseem
a5681.title: female Kabul resident
a5681.speech: “There is no good memory of the past one year. I have to think twice what to wear before stepping out to avoid a beating by Taliban.” ; “It also hurts to see that girls cannot go to schools, which is part of a normal life anywhere. Taliban is using religion just to prevent women from progressing.”

a5681.speaker: Zabihullah Mujahid, Taliban spokesman
a5681.name: Zabihullah Mujahid
a5681.title: Taliban spokesman
a5681.speech: Claimed last week there had been “major achievements” in the past year: “Afghans are no more being killed in war, foreign forces have withdrawn, and security has improved,” he told reporters.

a5843.speaker: Organizers of the seminar (FONAC and USAID/WACSI-Benin)
a5843.name: Organizers of the seminar (FONAC and USAID/WACSI-Benin)
a5843.speech: Observed that African countries in general, and Benin in particular, have for some decades been confronted with transnational organized crime.

a5843.speaker: Kevin Armstrong, Director of USAID Benin
a5843.name: Kevin Armstrong
a5843.title: Director of USAID Benin
a5843.speech: Notes that the training will make it possible to strengthen cooperation among the various actors in the fight and to help lay the foundations for smooth communication among them. He hopes that thanks to WACSI, civil society organizations will intensify awareness-raising by all and will communicate with the public on questions linked to transnational organized crime, including corruption, with a view to holding members of the government and the authorities of state institutions accountable, in order to bring them to ensure transparency and integrity in their respective sectors.

a5843.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Elias, President of FONAC
a5843.name: Jean-Baptiste Elias
a5843.title: President of FONAC
a5843.speech: Indicated that this seminar should bring about the mobilization of national opinion on the threats caused by transnational organized crime to good governance and the economic development of the West African sub-region, and help lay the groundwork for good sub-regional cooperation between state and non-state actors in the fight.

a5843.speaker: Fortune Luc Olivier Guezo, Secretary General of the Ministry of Justice of Benin
a5843.name: Fortune Luc Olivier Guezo
a5843.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Justice of Benin
a5843.speech: Asserts that it could not be otherwise, and suggests that the gravity of transnational organized crime and its impacts on the socio-economic development of nations require that urgent and substantial actions be undertaken to prevent and wage a fierce fight against these scourges. He judges it urgent to combat them through education, awareness-raising and the training of actors, then to ensure the application of the laws in force, while emphasizing international cooperation. He indicates that the context of growing insecurity in the cities and at the borders calls for this, and reports that in recent years criminal activities have developed considerably, taking on a worrying scale reflected in the diversification and rapid expansion of illicit activities by criminal groups and the increase in the number of countries affected, all of it well supported by corruption.

a6011.speaker: South Africa (case filed at the International Court of Justice)
a6011.name: South Africa (case filed at the International Court of Justice)
a6011.speech: Filed its case on December 29, accusing Israel of genocide and violation of the United Nations Genocide Convention with its actions in the Gaza Strip since October 7.

a6011.speaker: Joan Donoghue, President of the International Court of Justice
a6011.name: Joan Donoghue
a6011.title: President of the International Court of Justice
a6011.speech: On Friday ordered the immediate release of all those held hostage by the Hamas militants during the invasion of Israeli territory on October 7, 2023 ; Said that South Africa had standing to submit a genocide case against Israel regarding its war in Gaza.

a6011.speaker: International Court of Justice (ruling)
a6011.name: International Court of Justice (ruling)
a6011.speech: Said the continual abduction of people captured by Hamas militants during the October attack was no longer justifiable and ordered that all of them should be released immediately and without any conditions: "The order then states that the court deems it necessary to emphasise that all parties to the conflict in the Gaza Strip are bound by international humanitarian law. It is gravely concerned about the fate of the hostages abducted during the attack in Israel on 7 October 2023 and held since then. By Hamas and other armed groups and calls for their immediate and unconditional release."

a6011.speaker: International Court of Justice (ruling)
a6011.name: International Court of Justice (ruling)
a6011.speech: Mandated the Israeli authorities to allow the people of Gaza uninterrupted access to medical needs and humanitarian assistance: "The court is also the view that Israel must take measures in its power to prevent and punish a direct and public incitement to commit genocide in relation to the members of the Palestinian group in the Gaza Strip. The court further considers that Israel must take immediate and effective measures to enable the provision of urgently needed basic services and humanitarian assistance to address the adverse conditions of life faced by Palestinians in the Gaza Strip." ; "Israel must also take effective measures to prevent the destruction and ensure the preservation of evidence related to allegations of acts within the scope of Article 2 and Article Three of the Genocide Convention against members of the Palestinian group in the Gaza Strip."

a6361.speaker: Uche Ejesieme, spokesman for the Nigerian Customs Service
a6361.name: Uche Ejesieme
a6361.title: spokesman for the Nigerian Customs Service
a6361.speech: According to the customs spokesman, Uche Ejesieme, the details of the discovery will be made public as soon as possible.

a6361.speaker: Law enforcement authorities (Nigeria)
a6361.name: Law enforcement authorities (Nigeria)
a6361.speech: The full inventory of the weapons has not yet been completed, but according to law enforcement, the ammunition could arm an entire battalion.

a6409.speaker: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria (directive to the new NNPC Ltd board)
a6409.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria (directive to the new NNPC Ltd board)
a6409.speech: "Restructuring is crucial for enhancing operational efficiency, restoring investor confidence, boosting local content, driving economic growth, and advancing gas commercialisation and diversification."

a6409.speaker: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria (directive to the new NNPC Ltd board)
a6409.name: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria (directive to the new NNPC Ltd board)
a6409.speech: "Conduct a strategic portfolio review of NNPC-operated and Joint Venture assets to ensure alignment with value maximisation objectives."

a6551.speaker: 2025 Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC), produced by the Food Security Information Network
a6551.name: 2025 Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC)
a6551.title: produced by the Food Security Information Network
a6551.speech: Projections show that at least 6.8 million people, representing 33 percent of Malawi's population, are struggling to meet their basic needs, especially finding food; of the 6.8 million, 5.7 million were in IPC phase three, meaning they faced a more severe level of acute food insecurity, with households experiencing significant limitations in food access and coping strategies ; "An analysis on Malawi showed that while some macroeconomic impacts, especially losses in foreign exchange, may be mitigated by policy measures, the broader decline in welfare is likely to have far-reaching effects, including increases in poverty and malnourishment." ; "Reductions in official direct assistance—and the associated foreign exchange—also pose broader macroeconomic risks, undermining fiscal capacity and threatening currency stability and access to essential imports." ; The report said that in Malawi, as in other countries, financial allocations primarily target the symptoms of food crises, rather than mitigating their drivers or the structural factors that increase vulnerability and limit capacities to recover, indicating that a protracted food crisis in Malawi has been in all nine editions of the GRFC.

a6551.speaker: Preliminary crop production estimates for the 2024/25 agriculture season
a6551.name: Preliminary crop production estimates for the 2024/25 agriculture season
a6551.speech: Indicate that Malawi faces another maize deficit, with data showing that 2,962,620 metric tonnes of the staple grain will be harvested against a national requirement of 3.5 million MT.

a6551.speaker: Leonard Chimwaza, agriculture extension specialist
a6551.name: Leonard Chimwaza
a6551.title: agriculture extension specialist
a6551.speech: Reacting to the report, stressed the need to maximise production from mega farms. He said prudence in the selection of productive farmers, timely engagement of input suppliers, adoption of mechanisation, timely distribution of inputs and total adoption of climate-smart agriculture practices can help turnaround the fortunes ; "Government should strengthen policies that promote climate smart agriculture, diversifying crop varieties, irrigation and smallscale livestock production. We need to improve storage systems in order to ensure that food supplies last. In the short term, Admarc must ensure steady supply and have a balanced distribution matrix which could assist in ensuring steady availability of the maize in its depot across the country. Relief maize is also key for those who cannot afford to buy."

a6551.speaker: Sam Kawale, Minister of Agriculture of Malawi
a6551.name: Sam Kawale
a6551.title: Minister of Agriculture of Malawi
a6551.speech: Conceded that the challenges of food security are real and said government was taking bold steps to find long-term solutions to have a hunger-free future. He said in the short-term, the Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma) will continue distributing free food to vulnerable households, and are expanding the programme to ensure no one is left behind. Kawale also said the Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation (Admarc) has received increased funding to purchase and sell maize at subsidised prices, ensuring affordability for all Malawians ; "We are investing close to K100 billion in irrigation projects this year alone. This includes fertiliser, seeds and pest control support for farmers in irrigation schemes."

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.speech: Warned today that Nigeria, Kenya, Somalia and South Sudan will run out of stocks of therapeutic foods within the next three months.

a6636.speaker: Main international humanitarian organisations
a6636.name: Main international humanitarian organisations
a6636.speech: Condemned in unison this Friday the situation in the Gaza Strip following the official declaration of a state of famine in Gaza City and its surroundings, denouncing “famine in full view of the world”.

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.speech: Said today that it estimates that another million children in Nigeria will suffer from acute malnutrition by April 2025, thus totalling around 5.4 million minors in this situation.

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.speech: Reported today that the number of Sudanese children facing severe food shortages has almost doubled in six months and that 75% of them suffer daily from a lack of food, with the war aggravating this situation.

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.speech: Warned today that around 1.1 million Palestinian children living in the Gaza Strip could die of hunger or from disease.

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a6636.speech: According to the organisation, more than 1,200 people are reported to have died this year in Southern and Eastern Africa in natural disasters associated with climate change.

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (report entitled “Stop the war on children”)
a6636.name: Save the Children (report entitled “Stop the war on children”)
a6636.speech: According to the report presented today, about 420 million children live in areas affected by armed conflict, 30 million more than in 2016.

a6636.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a6636.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a6636.speech: Warned today in a statement of the need for new entry points for humanitarian aid in Yemen to avert famine in the war-torn country.

a6636.speaker: Save the Children (report)
a6636.name: Save the Children (report)
a6636.speech: A report by the organisation released today indicates that six African nations are among the 10 worst in the world for being a child in a war zone.

a6748.speaker: Mustafa Duhulow, Director General of the Immigration and Citizenship Agency (ICA)
a6748.name: Mustafa Duhulow
a6748.title: Director General of the Immigration and Citizenship Agency (ICA)
a6748.speech: Emphasized the urgency of improving service delivery and cracking down on trafficking networks: "We must accelerate our efforts against illegal migration and human trafficking. Relevant departments must remain vigilant to protect Somali youth and prevent traffickers from exploiting vulnerable individuals," Duhulow said in a statement.

a6748.speaker: Senior officials from the Citizenship, Investigation and Border Management departments (unnamed)
a6748.name: Senior officials from the Citizenship
a6748.title: Investigation and Border Management departments (unnamed)
a6748.speech: Presented reports detailing the challenges in passport recognition and measures needed to curb unlawful migration.

a6748.speaker: Artan Mohamed Artan, head of Mogadishu Border Control
a6748.name: Artan Mohamed Artan
a6748.title: head of Mogadishu Border Control
a6748.speech: Told Kaab TV that authorities have started intercepting individuals being trafficked through Aden Adde International Airport: "We regularly rescue young men and women who are in the hands of traffickers attempting to smuggle them through Libya and Algeria." According to Artan, some of those rescued have been reunited with their families, while officials closely monitor the travel of young people aged 19-25, the primary targets of traffickers.

a6748.speaker: U.S. Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report
a6748.name: U.S. Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report
a6748.speech: Consistently ranks Somalia among the lowest globally (Tier 3) due to the lack of anti-trafficking laws and weak enforcement.

a7176.speaker: Thomas Kazungu Karisa, petrol station attendant and farmer in Kilifi county, Kenya
a7176.name: Thomas Kazungu Karisa
a7176.title: petrol station attendant and farmer in Kilifi county, Kenya
a7176.speech: Says his life was transformed by a cash donation from GiveDirectly ; “My family often went to bed hungry, my children were sent home from school for unpaid fees and I was buried in debt,” said Karisa, a father of five ; “If they had given me food, it would have been long gone by now” ; “But with the money, I have been able to change my life.”

a7176.speaker: GiveDirectly
a7176.name: GiveDirectly
a7176.speech: Believes charities and NGOs should stop handing out things like food and school books, and start just sending people cash ; With the United States and other Western countries sharply cutting aid in recent months, GiveDirectly believes cash handouts offer a way to do more with less ; Sees the risk that families may not spend cash in the right way as a selling point for giving cash wherever possible.

a7176.speaker: GiveDirectly
a7176.name: GiveDirectly
a7176.speech: Said fears the money would be misused or wasted were unfounded, noting it has given donations to almost 1.5 million Africans and carried out 25 studies across the continent to measure the impact ; Says 80 percent of donations goes directly into the hands of recipients, though it still has overhead costs.

a7176.speaker: One Kenyan study
a7176.name: One Kenyan study
a7176.speech: Found that families generated $2.50 for every $1 received.

a7176.speaker: Caroline Teti, GiveDirectly’s vice president for risk in Africa
a7176.name: Caroline Teti
a7176.title: GiveDirectly’s vice president for risk in Africa
a7176.speech: “We can show evidence of cash having reversed domestic violence, improved child mortality, improved business outcomes, made families healthier, children accessing more education.”

a7176.speaker: Caroline Teti, GiveDirectly’s vice president for risk in Africa
a7176.name: Caroline Teti
a7176.title: GiveDirectly’s vice president for risk in Africa
a7176.speech: “Cash is not a magic bullet,” Teti said. Governments are still needed for fundamentals like schools, health facilities and electricity. ; “Poverty doesn’t wait. One year is enough for a girl to drop out of school... for a mother or child to die.”

a7176.speaker: Caroline Teti, GiveDirectly’s vice president for risk in Africa
a7176.name: Caroline Teti
a7176.title: GiveDirectly’s vice president for risk in Africa
a7176.speech: “Lives can only be changed by the people who are living that life. We are giving them dignity and we are giving them choice.”

a7176.speaker: 2022 study by the University of Washington
a7176.name: 2022 study by the University of Washington
a7176.speech: Found that back-office costs in the United States ate up 30 to 60 percent of budgets for global health projects.

a7176.speaker: Tariq Riebl, Norwegian Refugee Council strategy and innovation director
a7176.name: Tariq Riebl
a7176.title: Norwegian Refugee Council strategy and innovation director
a7176.speech: Said the Norwegian Refugee Council now gives 20 percent of its aid in cash, but could easily give as much as 45 percent.

a7176.speaker: Tariq Riebl, Norwegian Refugee Council strategy and innovation director
a7176.name: Tariq Riebl
a7176.title: Norwegian Refugee Council strategy and innovation director
a7176.speech: Told AFP the only real obstacle is “latent conservatism” in the aid sector: “There’s something more comforting about handing over a kit of non-food items or a sack of rice, than giving cash.”

a7176.speaker: USAID policy paper (October)
a7176.name: USAID policy paper (October)
a7176.speech: Even USAID — before being gutted by the administration of President Donald Trump — finally backed the use of cash payments in a policy paper last October, after years of internal pushback.

a7176.speaker: Tarak Bach Baouab, MSF (Doctors Without Borders) advocacy head
a7176.name: Tarak Bach Baouab
a7176.title: MSF (Doctors Without Borders) advocacy head
a7176.speech: “Cash for healthcare remains very rare,” said MSF’s advocacy head. “We want to be sure of the quality of our programmes so we prefer sourcing the drugs and equipment ourselves.”

a7176.speaker: Tarak Bach Baouab, MSF (Doctors Without Borders) advocacy head
a7176.name: Tarak Bach Baouab
a7176.title: MSF (Doctors Without Borders) advocacy head
a7176.speech: “We’re not there to tell people what to do with their lives. It’s not very empowering and it creates a lot of dependency” ; “But if you give cash to a family and they don’t spend it in the right way, then we might see health outcomes diminish.”

a7326.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a7326.name: Daniel Chapo
a7326.title: President of Mozambique
a7326.speech: Announced that the country will today begin using a technological system to track medications and healthcare products, aimed at preventing drug theft: "As of today, Mozambique begins the official implementation of the national traceability system for medicines and healthcare products. Starting today, medicines will have a tracking seal from manufacture to the patient" ; according to the head of state the initiative is part of a government strategy for what he called "health sovereignty", which aims to free the country from constrained access to pharmaceutical products, especially in times of crisis where there are shortages ; "Even if a medicine is opened outside the country, or if it is smuggled, the system will register it in Mozambique and indicate its location. We are thus taking a historic step toward ensuring that every medicine for Mozambican citizens is safe, traceable, and authentic in terms of quality" ; also explained that the system aims to strengthen the fight against smuggling, theft, the diversion of medicines and counterfeiting ; "It's a system that will allow savings not only for the Mozambican state, but also for all local importing industries, pharmacies, and other stakeholders in the legitimate medicine supply chain, as everyone will have visibility of their stocks throughout the supply chain, from the factory to the patient."

a7326.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a7326.name: Daniel Chapo
a7326.title: President of Mozambique
a7326.speech: In anticipation of the event, President Chapo had announced that the Mozambican government is working with national and foreign investors and researchers to ensure local production of medicines, reducing external dependence.

a7326.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a7326.name: Government of Mozambique
a7326.speech: On May 11, the Mozambican government announced that it would introduce an electronic system to control medicines in the national health system to prevent theft and promised to expel any professionals in the sector found stealing them.

a7326.speaker: Ussene Isse, Health Minister of Mozambique
a7326.name: Ussene Isse
a7326.title: Health Minister of Mozambique
a7326.speech: "I must publicly assure you, regarding the issue of medicine theft in the health system, that there will be no compromise, zero tolerance. Those found stealing medicines and who are employees of the Ministry of Health will not be allowed to work in the national health system. Zero tolerance means expulsion; there is no negotiation possible," Health Minister Ussene Isse promised at the time.

a7326.speaker: National Medicines Regulatory Authority (ANARME), promoter of MIH Expo-24
a7326.name: National Medicines Regulatory Authority (ANARME)
a7326.title: promoter of MIH Expo-24
a7326.speech: According to its promoter ANARME, MIH Expo-24 "is a comprehensive platform to present a unified international effort to strengthen health systems against climate-related risks, while promoting initiatives that drive the sector toward net-zero environmental impact."

a7332.speaker: Christo Visser, Electricity Pricing and Financial Modelings Senior Manager at NamPower
a7332.name: Christo Visser
a7332.title: Electricity Pricing and Financial Modelings Senior Manager at NamPower
a7332.speech: Says the 17.44% they applied for from the electricity control board is 33% below their operational cost; says they require about N$2 billion for the year 2026. "But in our tariff application, we only applied for 1,73 billion that is 33% less so we only recover 67% of the cost. It's the same with maintenance on your vehicle; you can skip a service, and nothing will happen, but some other time, it's gonna catch up with you."

a7332.speaker: Desdemona Lubinda, NamPower's Head of Electricity Pricing
a7332.name: Desdemona Lubinda
a7332.title: NamPower's Head of Electricity Pricing
a7332.speech: Explained that, with no tariff increment last year, the increment they required was to rectify the skipped tariff increment.

a7332.speaker: Pinehas Mutota, Electricity Control Board's Economic and Market Regulation Executive
a7332.name: Pinehas Mutota
a7332.title: Electricity Control Board's Economic and Market Regulation Executive
a7332.speech: Said the ECB's role is to balance the interests of the consumers with that of the electricity suppliers.

a7358.speaker: Ethiopian School Leaving Exam (matriculation) results
a7358.name: Ethiopian School Leaving Exam (matriculation) results
a7358.speech: The recently released results have brought to light stark deficiencies: from a staggering 845,000 students who appeared for the exam, a mere 3.2pc achieved passing grades, translating to only about 27,267 students, and 42.8pc of the 3,106 schools that sat their students for the exams reported zero passes; only five schools celebrated a 100pc pass rate and another five institutions reported pass rates exceeding 94.5pc; last year, of the 896,520 students who took the same national exam, only 3.3pc surpassed the 50pc mark.

a7358.speaker: Ministry of Education officials (Ethiopia)
a7358.name: Ministry of Education officials (Ethiopia)
a7358.speech: The Ministry’s officials have expressed their intent, pointing to the ongoing “transformational” reforms in the education sector, including the digitalisation of the Ethiopian School Leaving Exam and a push towards greater transparency around results; the Ministry, recognising the widening gap, has reversed its previous decision against remedial exams.

a7417.speaker: Valerie Amos, United Nations humanitarian chief
a7417.name: Valerie Amos
a7417.title: United Nations humanitarian chief
a7417.speech: Together with Commissioner Georgieva, expressed deep concern about the fate of the civilian populations affected by the prevailing instability in the Central African Republic and called for improved humanitarian access to people in urgent need of assistance: “It is the entire population of the country, 4.6 million people, that is affected by the crisis. Half of them are children. The needs are enormous and keep growing, with 1.6 million people in need of assistance,” she said in Bangui. “Security is a major concern and the UN is working hard to re-establish its presence and its activities in different parts of the country.” She expressed particular concern about the impact of this crisis on women and children.

a7417.speaker: Valerie Amos, United Nations humanitarian chief
a7417.name: Valerie Amos
a7417.title: United Nations humanitarian chief
a7417.speech: “Once again children are the first victims of the crisis. In CAR, thousands of them are suffering from acute malnutrition, have been displaced and are no longer at school because of the conflict.”

a7417.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva, European Commissioner for International Cooperation, Humanitarian Aid and Crisis Response
a7417.name: Kristalina Georgieva
a7417.title: European Commissioner for International Cooperation, Humanitarian Aid and Crisis Response
a7417.speech: “The Central African authorities must urgently restore the rule of law so that we can restore the flow of humanitarian aid. About 35 percent of the population finds itself in a particularly vulnerable situation and needs life-saving assistance. Today I am announcing additional funding of 8 million euros, which brings the EU’s financial contribution for CAR this year to 20 million. However, the international community must do more, and I call on them to do everything possible to help put an end to the suffering of the Central African population.”

a7417.speaker: Valerie Amos and Kristalina Georgieva
a7417.name: Valerie Amos and Kristalina Georgieva
a7417.speech: Met the transitional president, Michel Nondokro Djotodia, as well as members of the transitional government, and urged the authorities to ensure that humanitarian organisations can carry out their programmes.
